title: Five Games Left for Max Anderson’s Tigers Debut
description: Tigers prospect Max Anderson stayed behind after Sunday's finale, and one roster decision stands in his way. #Tigers
fullText:
Detroit Tigers second base prospect Max Anderson spent the 2026 minor league season with the Toledo Mud Hens at the Triple-A level. In 113 games with Toledo this season, he hit .302 with 17 home runs and 61 RBIs, along with six stolen bases on eight attempts.

His on-base percentage was .386, his slugging percentage was .486 and his OPS was .872. Anderson, 24, has yet to play for the Tigers at the major league level.

Toledo's season ended Sunday with a 2-0 shutout of the Louisville Bats, so Anderson only plays again this year if Detroit puts him in a game. Emily Waldon, a Tigers prospect writer for Baseball America, reported on X on Sunday, "

There are just five games remaining for Detroit, and all five are at Comerica Park. The Tigers have two games left against the Washington Nationals and three against the Pittsburgh Pirates. With nothing left to play for, giving Anderson a look in a game or two would cost them nothing.

Anderson is not on the 40-man roster, which makes it harder for the Tigers to get him into a game this month. They may have to wait until next season, but there is very little downside to making the move now.

Katrina Stebbins of Motor City Bengals wrote:

"There's little to lose at this point. Their loss to the White Sox on Sunday night marked their elimination from postseason contention, rendering their last six games basically meaningless. That doesn't mean the Tigers can't have a little fun, though. They're probably letting Justin Verlander pitch against the Pirates on Saturday; why not add a debut on top?

The only thing that could be keeping the club from actually making the move is that Anderson isn't currently on the 40-man roster. But assuming that they want to save him from the Rule 5 draft this offseason (which they should), it might even behoove them to get the roster move out of the way early."

Playing Anderson now, instead of risking him in the Rule 5 draft, is the smart move. Detroit fans want to see what he can do. He is expected to be added to the 40-man roster this offseason, and he will have a chance to make the team out of spring training.

title: Bucky Irving And Jadarian Price Lead Our Must-Sit Fantasy Football Running Backs For Week 3
description: Our top must-sit fantasy football running backs for Week 3.
fullText:
We have reached Week 3, and it is time to set our lineups. The last thing you want is to end up with a dud in your lineup, especially in your running back slot.

That's why we are here to help you avoid any duds. These are the top running back sits for Week 3.

If Price plays, he will likely come into Week 3 at less than 100% after exiting Week 2 with a shoulder injury. However, even if he doesn't play, Emanuel Wilson is also a dangerous starting option.

The Washington Commanders have been surprisingly tough against fantasy running backs this season. They have allowed the fewest fantasy points to running backs this season at just 9.0 points per game. This is a situation we are looking to avoid, especially if Price is active. There is no way that we are starting a potentially limited running back in committee against the Commanders' rush defense.

Irving is off to a strong start to his season, racking up 134 rushing yards, 49 receiving yards, and a touchdown through two weeks. However, the Bucs offense looks broken, and they have a brutal matchup this week against the Minnesota Vikings.

Last week, the Vikings held the Bears and their elite rushing game to just three points. Despite having to go up against the Bears' rushing attack, the Vikings have allowed the fourth-fewest fantasy points to running backs at just 11.9 points per game. We are very concerned about Irving this week, along with everyone in the Buccaneers' offense.

This marks the third consecutive week that Lloyd has been featured as one of our must-sits in Week 3. Don't let a fluke touchdown in Week 2 get you excited about Lloyd because you're going to end up disappointed.

In Week 2, he played fewer snaps than Chris Brooks for the second consecutive week and matched Kaleb Johnson with just 16 offensive snaps. He also had fewer carries than Johnson, and through two games has been less efficient than both backs on the ground. His 3.3 yards per carry in Week 3 was the most efficient game of his career. Why anyone ever expected him to be good is beyond me.

Do not start Lloyd or anyone in this backfield until Josh Jacobs is back. The matchup this week is tough as well. While the Falcons have struggled mightily against the pass, they have actually allowed the sixth-fewest fantasy points to running backs so far this season.

JCM is going to be a matchup-based start, and we are not interested in starting him against the Seattle Seahawks defense. He has both a low floor and a low ceiling in this game.

With Jayden Daniels sidelined, he is going to have very limited touchdown upside, and he brings almost nothing in the passing game, totaling -2 receiving yards through two games. We don't see any viable reason to play him in this matchup with a backup quarterback under center.

title: Clemson, Georgia Cancel 4-Game Series in Football
description: Clemson and Georgia have mutually agreed to cancel the upcoming 4 game series between the two schools according to reporting by the Athens Banner-Herald. The news was discovered via an open records request this week, though the agreement was signed back in March. The Tigers and Bulldogs planned to play each other 4 times starting […]
fullText:
Clemson and Georgia have mutually agreed to cancel the upcoming 4 game series between the two schools according to reporting by the Athens Banner-Herald. The news was discovered via an open records request this week, though the agreement was signed back in March. The Tigers and Bulldogs planned to play each other 4 times starting in 2029 with games split between both schools.

This news isn't that surprising. Clemson entered into a 12 year agreement with Notre Dame followed by the ACC announcing a move to 9 conference games each year. Clemson's annual rivalry against South Carolina and the inherent desire to play a cupcake to get 7 home games meant any other P4 out of conference games were unlikely. Somehow teams are allergic to playing 12 P4 games.

Frankly this sucks. As we talked about when the Notre Dame series was announced, these moves now are all about money. The Notre Dame series is nice, but Clemson – Notre Dame doesn't have the tradition of Clemson – UGA or a host of other potential OOC matchups. Clemson "needs" 7 home games a year, that's impossible to do with all P4 OOC opponents, especially in years when Clemson will only have 4 home conference games.

At this point it is hard to say when, if ever, Clemson will play UGA again. Until there are drastic changes in conference scheduling, or the Notre Dame series is cancelled, the powers that be won't see space in the schedule for UGA. And it is a real shame. The recent revival of this series was great and something that should remain in college football.

title: Cubs $175M Alex Bregman contract decision called best move of 2026
description: This $175M decision by the Cubs has turned out incredibly well.
fullText:
Cubs $175M Alex Bregman contract decision called best move of 2026 originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

There were plenty of great moves made this offseason and during the 2026 season by the trade deadline. But the Chicago Cubs' roster move for one player might be the best.

While Pete Crow-Armstrong has dominated headlines for the right reasons, and the Cubs' rotation has dominated them for the wrong reasons, Alex Bregman has flown under the radar a bit for how good he's been with the Cubs.

ESPN's Jeff Passan called the $175 million contract for Bregman the "transaction of the year," thanks to how well Bregman has integrated into the Cubs' lineup and his second-half breakout.

"Transaction of the year: Alex Bregman," Passan writes. "... Bregman opted out of that deal, and while the market was kinder, the industry thought the Cubs wildly overpaid when they gave him five years and $175 million over the winter."

The five-year, $175M deal was dubbed an overpay at the time. But Bregman has proven those doubters wrong, though it did take some time to do so.

He posted a .689 OPS through July, and there was some real worry about whether he'd be the kind of contributor the Cubs could rely on.

But, since the beginning of August, Bregman has been on a tear. Across 46 games and 176 at-bats, Bregman has 15 home runs, 42 RBIs, 21 walks, just 23 strikeouts, a .295 batting average, and a 1.006 OPS.

MORE: How Mets, Dodgers and Guardians all made same brutal trade mistake amid MVP races

Unfortunately, Bregman was hit in the head by a foul ball and will miss some time, with a return in the postseason possible.

But the Cubs' decision to give him a five-year deal looks like an incredible one after Bregman's late-season resurgence.

While Bregman won't post a 1.006 OPS for the rest of that five-year deal, if he is around an .800 OPS hitter with good defense at third base, this signing will be quite the move for the Cubs as they try to make another World Series run.

title: The shocking Steelers stat exposing Aaron Rodgers’ third-down woes
description: Quarterback Aaron Rodgers sees his passer rating plummet from 81 on first down to a dismal 59 on third down for the Pittsburgh Steelers.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' offense is navigating a dangerous tightrope early in the season, as high-risk passing situations and protection breakdowns at left tackle are putting 40-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers in physical harm's way.

Through two games, Pittsburgh's inability to play as a cohesive unit has led to severe drops in quarterback performance in key situations. On a recent episode of the "Locked On Steelers" podcast, analyst Alan Saunders highlighted how early-down play selection is forcing Rodgers into uncomfortable passing downs.

"Aaron Rodgers has an 81 passer rating on first down, and that's not great, but it's 59 on third down," Saunders noted. "So, yeah, I think they throw more on first down."

When forced into third-and-long situations, Rodgers' execution has also faltered under pressure. Host Christopher Carter pointed to instances where Rodgers missed open options while forcing throws into coverage.

"Aaron Rodgers, I just felt that there were several plays where I thought that he didn't see what was available," Carter explained. "There was one play where he tried to force it to DK Metcalf when [Christian] Gonzalez was all over him. He had Roman Wilson wide open on the right side of the field."

Compounding those field-vision issues are severe pass-protection breakdowns along the edge. Left tackle Troy Fautanu has shown flashes of physical promise, but his catastrophic whiffs have exposed Rodgers to violent hits that threaten the team's entire season strategy.

"Look, if Troy Fautanu has another rep as bad as the one that, was it Christian Elliss, who breaks Rodgers in half, how many of those hits is Aaron Rodgers getting up from?" Saunders warned. "Right there, that could have been the season."

If head coach Mike McCarthy cannot scheme around these protection lapses and keep Rodgers out of third-and-long scenarios, the Steelers risk exposing their veteran quarterback to hits he simply cannot afford to take.

title: Red Sox remove interim tag, name Chad Tracy the franchise's 49th manager after historic turnaround
description: The Boston Red Sox have removed the interim tag and named Chad Tracy the 49th manager in team history.  The team announced the elevation on Tuesday, signing Tracy to a three-year contract that will run through the 2029 season, with a club option for 2030.  The Red Sox also announced that it has exercised the 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.
fullText:
The Boston Red Sox have removed the interim tag and named Chad Tracy the 49th manager in team history.

The team announced the elevation on Tuesday, signing Tracy to a three-year contract that will run through the 2029 season, with a club option for 2030. The Red Sox also announced that it has exercised the 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.

The elevation of the 41-year-old Tracy comes after the Red Sox secured a wild-card spot in the playoffs on Sunday. Tracy took over in April after former manager Alex Cora was fired following a 10-17 start to the season.

Tracy has since guided the Red Sox to a 74-55 record, which included a 15-game win streak that tied the franchise record. It's a remarkable turnaround for a team that was 32-46 and 15 1/2 games back in the AL East race on June 24.

title: Is Raiders RB Mike Washington a top fantasy football waiver wire add Week 3?
description: Raiders rookie Mike Washington may be a player to consider adding with the potential to turn explosive plays into great production for team managers.
fullText:
Las Vegas Raiders rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. may be a player that fantasy football team managers will want to consider adding to their teams ahead of Week 3. Washington is still the backup in the Raiders' offensive backfield, though starter Ashton Jeanty hurt his ankle against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2, making the former a player to have on the radar moving forward.

FantasyPros' Pat Fitzmaurice labeled Washington as being a top player to add off of the waiver wire in fantasy football, with an FAAB true value of $1.

"Jeanty tweaked his ankle on Sunday — the same one he injured during an August practice," Fitzmaurice said. "…Washington is unrostered in 56% of Yahoo leagues despite his fine preseason showing. Jeanty stakeholders might want to consider slapping on the cuffs."

Washington picked up right where he left off from the preseason with seven carries for 41 rushing yards in the Raiders' season opener, but had a quiet game in Week 2, recording seven rushing yards in the win over the Chargers. Washington is a big play waiting to happen, and is liable to put up starter numbers on a weekly basis with ample carries.

In the event that Jeanty has to miss time after he hurt his ankle on Sunday, Washington will be a great player to snag off of the waiver wire in fantasy football with the potential to put up huge numbers.

title: Pistons $155M contract decision gives major setback in Jalen Duren negotiations amid stalemate
description: The Detroit Pistons may have hurt every chance at getting to sign Jalen Duren, even to the contract he has wanted all summer. That is the dangerous game they played with another contract decision.
fullText:
Pistons $155M contract decision gives major setback in Jalen Duren negotiations amid stalemate originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Detroit Pistons and Jalen Duren have been the talk of the NBA this offseason as the contract saga continues to drag on. Duren is one of the best young centers in the game, but the Pistons haven't wanted to pay him that much throughout the summer.

The battle between the two sides has gone on for so long that Detroit made a rookie extension over the weekend. Ausar Thompson received an extension before Duren.

"Detroit Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

Charania recently revealed that the Pistons have given Duren a new lucrative contract offer. This one is worth his desired $200 million.

"The Pistons and Jalen Duren are at an impasse and it's highly up in the air and questionable as to whether he will be reporting and showing up for media day in just 7 days...over the course of this offseason, his offer from the Pistons has been around the $180 to $190M over 5 years range. And that has also included incentives like weight clauses to my understanding. And that has all played a part in this as well. And over the last several weeks been kind of quiet on this front. The sides have picked up communication. And I am told right now the Pistons offer to Jalen Duren is $200M over 5 years," Charania said.

While that would have worked a couple of weeks ago, the Thompson extension has now put a dent in the process.

"Detroit inking Thompson to a five-year, $155 million deal, which will begin paying him an average annual value of $31 million, added a layer to Duren's contract negotiations," The Athletic's Sam Amick wrote.

This continues to be a never-ending saga with the two sides still so far apart in negotiations. Detroit should have had this offer from the beginning, or at least when they realized how stubborn Duren's camp was going to be.

After not being the first rookie extension on the team this offseason, Duren is wanting more. At this point, Detroit should just find some value for the young center somewhere else before he accepts a qualifying offer.

title: Busters for Raiders Week 2 vs Chargers
description: It was an uneven performance for the Raiders in LA. These are the players who struggled at times to get it done.
fullText:
Though the Raiders came out with the win in the end, they didn't exactly cruise to victory. In fact, they were still very much in danger of losing this one in the final four minutes. And when that happens, there are typically a few performances or crucial mistakes that were the reason why. These are their stories.

Last week the big story was about how good his hands are. Then he goes out in this one and had four drops. FOUR. That along with his 2.3 yards per carry average and it was a very different day than he had in the opener. Upside down, in fact, considering he was Top Baller for that game and now he's Top Buster.

Two of the Raiders' three possessions in the first quarter stalled because of Jeanty. Their second possession, he dropped the ball on a short cross on third and three. The next possession came off an interception. First play was an 18-yard completion that put the Raiders in first and goal from the four-yard-line. And four consecutive plays, all to Jeanty yielded a total of two yards. He was stopped for a loss of two on first down, picked up three yards on second down, and one yard on third down to bring of fourth and goal from the two. Then he took the direct snap, and bobbled it, leading to him getting stuffed at the line for the turnover on downs.

Just before the half, the Raiders got a big completion from Kirk Cousins to Tre Tucker to put them at the LA 42-yard-line. Jeanty got one yard on first down, dropped another pass on second down, and got nothing on third down, which mean Matt Gay would have to come out and hit a career-long 59-yard field goal to get points on the drive. Luckily, he nailed it. Otherwise the Jeanty would have felt a lot of heat for that.

Midway through the fourth quarter, Jeanty had his biggest drop of all. The Raiders lined up in third and one needing to keep a drive alive to preserve their three-point lead. Jeanty came out of the backfield and was open just past the line to gain. Cousins threw a nice, easy ball right into his hands and...clank.

The Chargers got the ball back and began moving down the field on what was looking like potentially a game-winning drive. It was only by the grace of a fumble and recovery that it didn't. Otherwise everyone would be looking back at that fourth drop of his as what led to it. But even still, he was by far the biggest Buster in this game for the Raiders. Hopefully this fall to earth helps him in the long run.

Now here's a familiar sight. At least it was last season. Glaze held up well in the opener. The same can't be said for this one. He gave up his first sack in the first quarter that started a three-and-out. Then a possession stalled in the second quarter, beginning with him being flagged for holding and then ending with him just getting easily worked by Khalil Mack to give up the sack.

In the third quarter, he gave up a run stuff for no gain that nearly killed a drive, but the Raiders were able to pick up the third and long on the next play. Overall the Raiders line took a big step back in this one, but none moreso than Glaze.

Now, this one I was not expecting. Not after the utterly dominant performance by Linderbaum in the opener. He lost his block to get Jeanty tackled for a short gain and missed another block later that got Cousins smacked on a short completion. Then he had a false start on third and five that led to the Raiders having to go for it on fourth and one at their own 35. The next drive, he got beat to give up a tackle for a loss of four. And it was only because of an illegal hands to the face penalty that they were able to pick up the resulting third-and-long.

He was targeted three times and had just one catch for nine yards. He didn't even see a pass in the first half. Which is not a great sign for a guy who was supposed to be one of the Raiders' top free agent additions this season. Even worse is he dropped that first pass. The second, he just couldn't get open and the ball was knocked down. He actually caught the third pass at the end of the third quarter. And then didn't see a pass in the fourth.

Nailor is currently fifth on the Raiders in receptions. And that's with Brock Bowers not in the lineup. Nailor's four catches for 36 yards through two games puts him on pace for 34 catches for 252 yards on the season. That's even well below his career average, which isn't great.

This article originally appeared on Raiders Wire: Busters for Raiders Week 2 vs Chargers

title: Wales pick dads and sons for Wheelchair World Cup
description: Fathers and sons Martin and Matthew Turner and Gareth Ramsey and Sid Ramsey are named in Wales' squad for the 2026 Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup.
fullText:
Wales have named two pairs of fathers and sons - Martin and Matthew Turner and Gareth and Sid Ramsey - in their squad for the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup in Australia.

It is the first time a father and son have represented Wales together at a Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup and the first time that two such pairings have been named in one squad.

A father-and-son pair have featured in the Wales set-up previously, but never before on the World Cup stage.

Head coach Alan Caron included them in his 12-strong selection for the tournament that starts for Wales against England on Friday, 30 October in Wollongong.

Group games against Ireland and the United States follow at the same venue as the teams aim for the knockout stages.

Gareth Ramsey, John Berriman and Fionn McCabe - who turns 16 shortly before the competition - could make Wales debuts during the event.

Caron said: "Having two father-and-son combinations in the squad makes this World Cup particularly special.

"Gareth and Sid, and Martin and Matthew, have the opportunity to share something that very few players ever get to experience: representing Wales together at a World Cup.

"For John, Fionn and Gareth, the opportunity to make their Wales debuts at a World Cup would be something very special, while our experienced players will be vital in helping them and the rest of the squad through the tournament."

Wales have had to fundraise to help with the costs of taking the squad to Australia, with more than half of the £10,000 target donated so far.

Stuart Williams (Edinburgh Giants/North Wales Crusaders), Jodie Boyd-Ward (Leeds Rhinos), Andrew Higgins (Midlands Hurricanes), Lee Sargent (Midlands Hurricanes/Cardiff Blue Dragons), Jonathan Gill, Fionn McCabe, Martin Turner (all North Wales Crusaders), Gareth Ramsey, Sid Ramsey (both Sheffield Eagles), Matthew Turner (Wigan Warriors/North Wales Crusaders), Mark Williams (Wigan Warriors/South Wales Jets), John Berriman (York RLFC).

title: ‘Things I think’: Jaxson Dart injury, Rams give Giants a reality check
description: Monday night showed us that the Giants, while they are better, have a long way to go to become championship-caliber.
fullText:
The big thing everyone connected with the New York Giants is thinking about in the wake of Monday's lopsided 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams is the health of quarterback Jaxson Dart. The Giants appear to have dodged the worst possible news, with the expectation that imaging on Tuesday will confirm a sprained MCL.

Monday's outcome, though, exposed a number of things about the 2026 Giants that we have to talk about, and that they have to be concerned about. Let's look at some of the 'things I think' as the Giants try to move on and get ready for a Week 3 game against the Tennessee Titans.

"We'll know more when we find out more," Giants coach John Harbaugh said after the game.

Harbaugh did allow that there was "no question" that seeing Dart moving around on the sideline after the game and believing his injury wasn't season-ending was comforting.

"The fact that it's not that outcome that you're talking about, the devastating outcome, is really good news," he said.

Dart's injury had nothing to do with all of the ongoing chatter about him not being willing to protect himself by sliding or getting out of bounds when he runs, something he actually did do in Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys.

Dart got hurt in the pocket, which, thanks to the NFL rulebook, is actually the safest place for quarterbacks. There is nothing the rules can do, though, to prevent getting sandwiched between two pass rushers and getting your knee inverted in a manner in which it's not meant to bend.

Maybe Dart misses two weeks. Maybe he misses six. The Giants, driven hard by Harbaugh this spring and summer, are about to best tested in a way they hoped not to be this season.

Giants players have seen and dealt with injuries before. They were saying the right things after the game. Winstn did admit losing Dart was a "gut punch" in the moment.

"You get ready to play another one," Winston said of what the Giants do now. "You got another opponent and they don't care."

"We're going to continue to practice hard, get out there, be more intentional about what we've got to do, what we've got to accomplish. Rally around Jameis," said Malik Nabers.

"For us to come in here and … get punched in the face, you have to get back up and keep going," right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor said. "There's still 15 more rounds."

The bigger issue, beyond how long Dart will be out, is that Monday night exposed many truths about the 2026 Giants. Let's get to them.

I have been warning for months not to expect a New England Patriots-like turnaround from 4-13 one year to 13-4 and a Super Bowl-berth the next. The most optimistic outcome I could summon for the 2026 Giants when asked to make a prediction was 9-8. Yet, after an impressive season-opening victory over the Dallas Cowboys national analysts were jumping the bandwagon and fans were dreaming big dreams.

The Rams brought those out-sized expectations crashing down to earth.

Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams, Aaron Donald, Sean McVay and the rest of a supremely talented Rams' roster showed the Giants and a national football audience what a Super Bowl-contending teams looks like.

The floor has been raised with the accomplished John Harbaugh as head coach. The eventual ceiling? Unknown, but the Rams exposed a number of things that have to be dealt with to find out.

The Giants averaged 2.5 yards per rush Monday night. Through two games, they average 3.7 yards per carry, 22nd in the NFL. Take out Dart's 11 carries for 54 yards in Week 1, that average dips to 3.5 yards. The Giants' longest non-Dart run in two games is 13 yards.

The Giants are built to be a run-first team, and that has to get better.

After a turnover games the Giants the ball on the Rams' 11-yard line they ran four times (including a 3-yard loss negated by a Los Angeles penalty), got nowhere, and settled for a deflating field goal when down 14-0.

Do they have the interior blocking or the backs to make that better? Maybe, but they need to be better than they were Monday. The Andrew Thomas injury might complicate matters. The Giants were outclassed up front by the Rams. Plus, they had several plays where the timing and execution were off, with players running into each other.

The simple question is, where is it?

Per @NextGenStats the Rams had a pressure rate of 58.6% tonight.

The Giants, after all of their investment in the Edge group over the years, somehow ended up at 15.2%

The Giants have just one sack and five quarterback hits in two games. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson wants to rush just four, which isn't a horrible goal considering the state of the secondary, but through two games Dak Prescott and Matthew Stafford have stood in the pocket and done basically whatever they wanted to do.

The Giants' sack percentage of 1.52 is worse than every team in the league except the Miami Dolphins.

With Brian Burns injured, fixing that quickly won't be easy.

Who knew at the start of training camp that the Giants would miss Tae Banks as much as they did last night? Cornerbacks Colton Hood and Greg Newsome, along with safety Tyler Nubin, were not up to the task of defending Davante Adams. The linebackers and safeties weren't up to the task of covering tight end Terrance Ferguson.

There are no easy fixes. Dream about a Joey Porter trade if you must, but the Giants really need an offseason where they can add talent via free agency and the draft.

One week after an impressive performance vs. Dallas, the Giants allowed the Rams to run for 163 yards on 28 carries, 5.8 per rush. Through two games, the Giants are giving up 5.0 yards per rush, 28th in the NFL.

Talent-wise, this is another area the Giants are going to have to Band-Aid, duct-tape, and scheme around until they can get to the offseason and try to add more young talent.

It was disturbing to see 2025 second-round pick Darius Alexander, who simply does not seem to be improving as a run defender, inactive. The Giants used journeyman Josh Tupou, a practice squad player who appeared in six games with the Ravens the past two seasons, and C.J. Okoye, a Nigerian-born defensive tackle who knew nothing about football until 2023, instead of Alexander.

Not that long ago, the upcoming four games (vs. the Tennessee Titans, vs. the Arizona Cardinals, at the Washington Commanders, vs. the New Orleans Saints) was looked at a stretch where the Giants might be able to run off some victories.

Now? Maybe it is still a softer part of the schedule, but there isn't any certainty that the Giants will be able to take advantage of it.

Months of good vibes that began when Harbaugh was hired crumbled on Monday night with the Dart injury and the reality check provided by the Rams. The season, as Eluemunor indicated, will be defined by the next 15 rounds.

Do the Giants have the ability to punch back? We'll find out.

title: State of the NFC South: Week 2 recap
description: Good week for half of the NFC South
fullText:
The division had a better week overall: two teams won, while the other two struggled.

If you remember last week's edition, I said that the Bucs should win their Week 2 game against the Cleveland Browns. Well, funny thing. After a long weather delay on what should have been the game's final drive, the Bucs couldn't score, resulting in a 4-point loss to the Browns. This was an embarrassing loss; Deshaun Watson outplayed Baker Mayfield, and the defense really struggled.

Tampa Bay's season is far from over, but Todd Bowles' seat is on fire.

Now, to our first win from the division, my goodness, the Panthers destroyed the Falcons. We will get to Atlanta after this, but the Panthers won this game 34-3, and it was never really in doubt. Carolina's defense played really well, and Bryce Young continues to have a really great start to the season.

At the top of the division, Carolina plays the Browns next week, and just like last week with the Bucs, I'm guessing the Panthers will win.

Yeesh. Losing a game by 31 points is never great, but it was worse than the score says. The one bright spot was the Falcons' rushing attack, but they had to abandon it because of the score. The QB play, with Penix and Tua out, was downright horrible.

In Week 3, the Falcons will be getting Penix back against the Green Bay Packers, who are also struggling to start the season.

Back to winning, the Saints had the shock of the week. In a game nobody expected New Orleans to win, they beat the Baltimore Ravens, a Super Bowl contender. It wasn't a perfect game, far from it, but with Tyler Shough being confident all game, the defense holding Derrick Henry to under 100 rushing yards (insane), and Chase Young being a monster off the edge, the Saints stayed in the game all day. In the second half, they really controlled the momentum, and after some interesting decisions by the Ravens, it was over in Baltimore.

Their next game is against the 2-0 Raiders, who have had a strong start to the season under former Saints OC Klint Kubiak. This will be a very fun game.

title: Micah Parsons reacts to Jaxson Dart injury with emotional message
description: Green Bay Packers star edge rusher Micah Parsons may have felt a familiar sense of concern when he watched New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffer a knee injury on Monday. A hit during Dart’s first quarter passing attempt forced the New York Giants quarterback out of Monday’s matchup with the Los Angeles Rams. Dart [...]
fullText:
Green Bay Packers star edge rusher Micah Parsons may have felt a familiar sense of concern when he watched New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffer a knee injury on Monday.

A hit during Dart's first quarter passing attempt forced the New York Giants quarterback out of Monday's matchup with the Los Angeles Rams. Dart needed help leaving the field before the Giants announced that he would not return, and New York eventually fell 28-6. With Parsons still sidelined while recovering from his own knee injury, the Packers pass rusher took to X to respond after seeing Dart suffer the setback.

"I freaking hate injuries, man! I hate that they are a part of football!" wrote the Packers star on his post on X(formerly Twitter).

Dart is reportedly dealing with a suspected MCL sprain that could keep him sidelined for an extended stretch. Parsons can relate to the frustration of a major knee injury after tearing his ACL in Week 15 against the Denver Broncos. The 27-year-old had been enjoying a strong start to his first run with the Packers before the injury abruptly brought it to an end.

There has been speculation that the four time All Pro could make his return in Week 5 against the Chicago Bears or Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys. However, neither possibility has been confirmed, and the Packers have yet to provide a definitive timeline for his return.

The Packers will take on the Atlanta Falcons in Week 3 at home.

title: Apple Is Bringing Back an Apple Watch Feature It Took Away With watchOS 27
description: watchOS 27.2 makes it easy to switch apps again.
fullText:
Typically, software updates introduce new features rather than taking them away. So, when you install watchOS 27 on your compatible Apple Watch, you probably aren't surprised to see updates like Siri AI or a step counter on the watch face. But you might be taken aback by what's missing—a multitasking feature that your Apple Watch has had for years.

As reported by 9to5Mac, Apple quietly removed the app switcher from Apple Watches with watchOS 27. As a result, users running the beta over the summer, or those who updated in September, were likely confused when double-clicking the Digital Crown: On watchOS 26 and earlier, that gesture pulls up a menu with all open apps, similar to the app switcher on iPhone. This allows you to quickly return to a previously used app without needing to dive into the "honeycomb" main app menu.

With watchOS 27, that's no longer the case. Not only is the app switcher gone, but the honeycomb app menu has been sidelined. In their place, Apple is pushing its new "Dynamic app grid." When you press the Digital Crown once, you'll see this new menu, which features the apps Siri thinks you're most likely to use. That might include recently used apps, but also apps you frequently use, even if you haven't used them in a while.

That might prove to be useful. The honeycomb menu can certainly make apps difficult to find, especially if you have a lot of them on your watch. But replacing the app switcher entirely doesn't make much sense: There's no guarantee Siri is going to list the recently used app you want to use on the new menu, so you might be forced to manually hunt for it anyway, whereas with the app switcher, you could quickly bounce back to any app, provided you had opened it recently.

This isn't the only feature Apple removed with watchOS 27—the company also discontinued the Walkie-Talkie feature with the update. But it looks like it won't be gone for long.

It seems Apple is changing its mind (or coming to its senses): 9to5Mac recently spotted that the app switcher is back as of the watchOS 27.2 beta. Apple didn't make a note of the addition in any changelogs, so it's unclear why the company undid the change, but it's a welcome recursion—though at this point, there's no guarantee it will make it to the official build of watchOS 27.2. If you're hoping for similar news about Walkie-Talkie, unfortunately that feature has officially been discontinued, so don't expect to see it in a future update.

Speaking of which, the only way to try watchOS 27.2 now is to install the watchOS beta on your Apple Watch. That's a risky venture, since you can't downgrade back to watchOS 27 if something goes wrong. Still, if you're really missing the app switcher, you can get it back by enrolling your watch in Apple's beta.

title: Peloton Just Launched Its First Foldable and Most Affordable Treadmill to Date
description: Peloton's new treadmills span a wide range, from a space-saving $2,195 foldable to a $6,695 powerhouse.
fullText:
Peloton just launched three new treadmills: the Tread Flex, its first folding treadmill, plus the Tread Vision and Tread+ Vision. Together they span a wide range, from a space-saving $2,195 machine for walkers to a $6,695 slat-belt powerhouse built for elite athletes and Hyrox competitors.

As with nearly every other market right now, there's a big focus on intelligence and personalization. Peloton claims the new hardware is "smarter," with features like a movement-tracking camera that can analyze your running form. The software goes further, with features that adapt to how you actually train, and what's really exciting is that many of them are coming to Peloton's existing treads too. I got a sneak peek at the lineup at Peloton Studios New York last week. Here's what I learned about Peloton's newest lineup of treadmills.

For most people, the Flex is the main headline here. It folds down to save roughly 50% of floor space, and folded, Peloton reps told me it's shorter than a Peloton Bike. A two-step cylinder release lowers the deck gradually, and a safety locking pin keeps it secure when upright. Caster wheels make it easy to reposition, and the swivel screen lets you move from the belt to floor workouts like strength, yoga, and stretching. It's also quiet: Peloton says it runs at 70 dB at 12.5 mph, its top speed, with no one on the belt. It's best suited to walkers, hikers, and low-impact cardio fans.

This is a top-to-bottom upgrade of Peloton's tread, with improvements at nearly every touchpoint:

A 23.8" swivel screen with Sonos-tuned speakers and an integrated cooling fan

A movement-tracking camera that powers Run Analysis and connected strength workouts

New deck cushioning with internal dampeners to reduce joint impact

A redesigned tray for your phone, tablet, and water bottle

New Jump Buttons that take you to the next or previous whole-number speed or incline in a single tap

Peloton pitches it at mixed households with varied goals: walkers, joggers, runners, and strength trainers.

The Tread+ Vision is Peloton's premium performance treadmill, built for high-mileage training and elite athletes. Its rubberized slat-belt deck rides on a ball-bearing system designed to return energy to your stride. It includes everything on the Tread Vision, including the movement-tracking camera for Run Analysis and connected strength workouts, plus the Jump Buttons, and adds exclusive Sled Mode and Free Mode (more on those below). Peloton says it's best for performance runners, endurance athletes, and Hyrox competitors.

For me, the bigger news is the launch of a slew of promising new software features. These are the ones that most caught my attention, especially because they're coming to legacy devices too, as long as the hardware can support them.

Run Analysis uses the movement-tracking camera for AI-powered form analysis. It measures cadence, vertical oscillation, stride length, and vertical ratio, then gives you a Running Efficiency Score from 1 to 100 after each workout, along with personalized tips. It needs a one-time camera calibration, and the camera runs silently in the background with no live display. It's available on the Tread Vision, Tread+ Vision, and CTS Tread+, but not in Bootcamp, Warm Up, Cool Down, or ReRun workouts.

IQ Pace Targets are coming to all tread hardware. It analyzes your recent running to recommend a personalized pace range, kicking in after about 10 running workouts and adapting as your fitness changes. On-screen Shortcuts line up instructor cues with your own targets, so a single tap changes your speed or incline. Personalization must be enabled.

ReRuns brings your real-world outdoor routes to the tread. It syncs past runs and walks from the Peloton app or a connected smartwatch, and Auto-Incline follows the actual elevation profile. If you haven't saved any run outdoors, there's a preloaded library that includes TCS New York City Marathon route segments and select past Peloton Run Club routes. Location services must be on during outdoor workouts.

Sled Mode is for the Hyrox crowd and is coming to all Tread+ hardware. It emulates the sled push with software-controlled resistance from 30 to 300 lbs against the slat belt. Press the "Free Mode" button, set your sled weight with the adjuster, and the belt is driven by your own stride. There are dedicated instructed Sled Mode classes, and it's also accessible in Just Run.

Heart rate workouts are Zone 2-based, non-instructed sessions guided by heart rate rather than speed or incline. They're available in Just Run and Entertainment, with real-time on-screen target zone guidance that adapts to keep you in the right zone. You'll need a connected heart rate monitor, smartwatch, or wearable. They work across all Peloton cardio hardware (Tread, Bike, and Row).

For all the new software features I list above, you'll need All-Access Membership—except heart rate workouts, which are also available on App+ and App.

title: FAW chief Mooney challenges Infantino's Fifa reform claims
description: Football Association of Wales chief executive Noel Mooney challenges suggestions Fifa is planning major reforms.
fullText:
Football Association of Wales chief executive Noel Mooney has played down suggestions Fifa is planning major reforms.

Fifa president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how world football's governing body operates and says he is open to reform.

In a letter sent to members of the Fifa Council and all of its national associations, Infantino explains the independent process would "recommend potential improvements".

"I've seen the headlines today about major reform at Fifa - that's not how the letter read to me, to be frank," Mooney said.

"I saw the letter itself that was sent out, it doesn't actually say reform of Fifa itself.

"It talks about reform around strategic projects and initiatives.

"They would look at how they were consulted and how decisions were made around that."

Infantino says he is open to talks over Fifa reform

FAW chief calls for Infantino to step down

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

That would have involved selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, and it sparked a major backlash.

The Welsh governing body was among the first national associations to withdraw backing for Infantino's bid to continue his leadership of Fifa.

Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

Mooney reiterated the FAW would not be endorsing Infantino's candidature.

"With the Fifa president, you're looking for a moral guardian of the game," Mooney told the BBC Radio Wales Phone In.

"You're not looking for somebody to sell off parts of the game.

"The World Cup does not need private equity. They have billions and billions of dollars in reserve.

"Give us the money. Let us build the pitches. You've got loads of reserves. Let's have it as soon as possible.

"There was a summit in Miami before as the World Cup kicked off, a meeting of all 211 federations.

"I stood up at that meeting and said, look, I mean, the revenue for Qatar was around eight billion.

"The revenue for this World Cup in Canada, USA and Mexico is 16 billion. Therefore, it's 100% increase in revenue, give us 100% growth."

title: India avoid shock defeat by Japan after controversial wide
description: World Champions India avoid a shock defeat in the one-off T20 against Japan after a wide ball is controversially overturned in the final over.
fullText:
One-off T20, Sano Cricket Ground

India 32-4 (5 overs): Iyer 16 (12); Hara-Hinze 2-17

Japan 30-3 (5 overs): Kadowaki-Fleming 12 (12); Washington 2-13

World champions India avoided a shock defeat by Japan with a tense two-run win after a wide ball was controversially overturned in the final over.

In the one-off T20, which was reduced to five overs a side, Japan needed eight off the final over after their bowlers had remarkably restricted cricketing juggernauts India to 32-4.

Left-hander Alexander Shirai-Patmore was attempting to reverse-sweep spinner Axar Patel, who bowled the ball down the leg side - which would have been the batter's off side had he been attempting a conventional shot - and the umpire called it a wide.

After the umpire's signal, Axar was visibly frustrated with the decision and disputed the call alongside captain Shreyas Iyer.

The two umpires had a discussion after India's complaints and the decision was overturned, significantly taking the equation to six runs needed off three balls instead of five off four.

Axar then closed out the over to finish with figures of 0-7 off two overs and Japan finished agonisingly short on 30-3.

In white-ball cricket, any delivery bowled down the leg side is usually called a wide, but the ICC's playing conditions for men's T20 internationals state a batter loses those privileges from the moment he or she changes the position of their hands or feet to play a reversed shot.

In the conditions, it says a wide should be called "if the ball passes wide of where the striker is standing, and which also would have passed wide of the striker standing in a normal batting position".

This suggests the correct decision was reached eventually, but the incident has gained attention for how it was overturned despite there being no decision review system (DRS) in place for the match.

The preamble for the playing conditions also refers to the "spirit of cricket", with "accept the umpire's decision" listed as one of these points, although this is not one of the game's laws.

It was an agonising near-miss for Japan, who had struggled early on in their chase as they stuttered to 8-2 after two overs before taking 17 off the next two, which kept them in contention before the dramatic finale.

With the ball, they were led by 17-year-old spinner Charlie Hara-Hinze who took 2-17, including the wicket of destructive opener Abhishek Sharma first ball, before Shreyas' 16 off 12 balls provided some relief from his side being 14-3.

It was the first time the teams had played each other internationally because Japan have never reached a T20 World Cup, and the game was played in preparation for the men's Asian Games which start on 24 September.

Earlier, India cruised to victory in the women's Asian Games final as they thrashed Sri Lanka by 147 runs.

title: 'In another galaxy' - La Liga chief dismisses Real's ref conspiracy claims
description: La Liga president Javier Tebas says claiming there is a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid is like "living in another galaxy".
fullText:
La Liga president Javier Tebas says claiming there is a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid is like "living in another galaxy".

Real manager Jose Mourinho accused officials of making key errors after his side were beaten 2-1 by rivals Atletico Madrid last week.

Mourinho brought printouts of screenshots to the post-match news conference, claiming Atletico should have been given two red cards in the first half.

Writing in response to an article in the Spanish media which claimed there is a "conspiracy" against Real, Tebes dismissed the allegations.

"Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy," Tebas said on social media.

"That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.

"It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch."

Real are fourth in La Liga, six points behind Barcelona who top the table on 21 points after winning all seven of their league games this season.

After defeat by Atletico, where Real went down to 10 men in a feisty encounter after defender Dean Huijsen was sent off, Mourinho blamed the officiating.

"We can skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," Mourinho said as he showed media the printed images.

"Those were two clear red cards. Given the difficulties we faced afterwards playing 11 against 10, we can only imagine what 50 minutes of 11 against nine would have been like."

Tebas has been critical of Real and its president Florentino Perez in previous years after disagreeing with their plans to join a European Super League in 2021.

In 2025 he said Real had "lost their head" after the club sent a formal letter of complaint to the Spanish FA about officiating in the league.

title: Pollock left money on table to stay at Saints - Hearn
description: Henry Pollock turned down rival offers worth much more than his Northampton extension, which will earn him over £400,000 a year, says adviser Eddie Hearn.
fullText:
Henry Pollock turned down rival offers worth hundreds of thousands of pounds more than his extension to stay at boyhood club Northampton, says Eddie Hearn.

Hearn, whose Matchroom promotional empire is centred on boxing, darts and snooker, has been working as Pollock's adviser since March.

Pollock, 21, has agreed a new deal with Saints that extends his terms to summer 2028 and is worth more than £400,000 a year.

"There were a couple of domestic offers – a couple of Prem offers - and international offers as well," said Hearn of Pollock's options during his renegotiation.

"We had a very, very straight conversation. I said to him, 'be honest, do you want to go?' And he went, 'no, I really don't want to go'. And that was it.

"He knew the numbers, but ultimately he just wanted to stay at the club.

"He left a lot of money on the table to stay with Northampton. But it wasn't even a tough decision for him."

Hearn says that some of Pollock's suitors were offering "well in excess of seven figures".

The £1m mark was where Hearn valued Pollock's annual salary prospects in an interview with the Daily Telegraph interview in August., external

Hearn acknowledges that his client's new deal "didn't quite get to the number" that was targeted.

The headline basic figure Pollock has accepted does not account for a signing bonus and various payments he receives for off-pitch work.

And Hearn says that Pollock's endorsement deals have carried him comfortably over £1m in total annual earnings.

"Everybody from major financial institutions to household brands to performance brands to nutritional brands to wellness brands… I mean, there isn't really a sector that hasn't hasn't approached us about Henry Pollock," said Hearn.

Pollock is keen to explore the possibility of representing Great Britain in rugby sevens at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

GB's qualification is far from certain after the programme went part-time and the team slipped from the top tier of the international circuit.

The back row's new deal does not include the sort of dedicated time to train up for sevens that France captain Antoine Dupont took before Paris 2024, but the prospect has been raised with Saints.

"Our principal obligation is to perform for Northampton and to help them win championships," said Hearn.

"Part of the arrangement allows him to look at those kind of opportunities, but only with a sensible conversation with the club."

Pollock's ability to maximise his on-pitch earnings in England is restricted by a £6.4m salary cap for Prem clubs.

Each team is allowed one player whose salary is exempt from the calculations; however, players who move between top-tier teams can only qualify for such marquee status after two years with their new side.

Hearn would scrap the cap entirely.

"Let the players earn," he said. "All they hear about is salary caps or one star player per team - marquee names or whatever you want to call it. You don't want that.

"You want to say to a young player, 'hey, come to rugby, you can be a superstar and you can earn a fortune'.

"You could have lost Pollock and it would have been a disaster for English rugby."

The salary cap is designed to make the Prem sustainable and competitive, with similar systems in place in most major American sports.

Players such as Pollock can supplement club earnings with a central England contract, worth about £150,000 a year, or one-off Test match fees.

Still, some England players, such as Jack Willis, Kyle Sinckler and Sam Simmonds, have left for France's Top 14 where a salary cap of 11m euros (£9.4m) offers scope for greater earnings.

Hearn's current stable of rugby stars is only two strong. Bath and Scotland fly-half Finn Russell is similarly represented by Matchroom in off-pitch matters and advised by Hearn.

However, Hearn has ambitions to become more deeply involved in the staging and promotion of the game. He is set to meet with Prem Rugby chief executive Simon Massie-Taylor in Monaco in the coming weeks to discuss ideas.

"We haven't really touched the surface in terms of what we could do in the sport," said Hearn.

"All I've done is done a few deals with Henry, he's come to a couple of fights and I've done a couple of Zoom calls [with journalists].

"That just shows you the buzz that can be created with a little bit of hype and perception.

"But hype and perception are nothing without substance. The sport and the brand is the substance and it's significant in rugby.

"Look at what Matchroom has done elsewhere. Boxing was dead, darts was non-existent, snooker was stuck in the air. We don't fail. Our track record is second to none.

"If we went into rugby, it would be a stroll in the park for me. It's a huge global sport steeped in history with fantastic values and tradition that just needs to be just turbo-charged."

title: Neutral venues and no 'away' fans - how Israel v Republic of Ireland became so contentious
description: BBC Sport explores the backdrop to the Republic of Ireland's matches against Israel, amid fraught tensions between the nations.
fullText:
An elite-level European football match will be played on Sunday at a neutral stadium, with no 'away' fans, and reduced television coverage.

That the match is even taking place had been in doubt - one side had to vote on a motion confirming whether or not they would participate amid significant opposition from fans, pundits and politicians.

But the vote confirmed the fixture would go ahead, and now the Republic of Ireland will travel to Debrecen, Hungary, for a Uefa Nations League 'away' match against Israel, played against a backdrop of ongoing and increasingly volatile disagreement between the two countries about Israel's military offensive in Gaza.

And on 4 October, the Republic of Ireland will face the same opponents in a 'home' match in Backa Topola - a small town in Serbia.

No tickets have been sold to Irish fans for either fixture, and Irish public broadcaster RTE will air a stripped-back version of match coverage, with no commentators, pundits, or half-time analysis.

So how did a Uefa Nations League match become one of the most contentious fixtures in football?

As soon as the Republic of Ireland were placed with Israel - plus Austria and Kosovo - at the Nations League draw in February, the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) faced calls from some to boycott the matches because of Israel's military action in Gaza.

In May a friendly match the Republic of Ireland played against Qatar in Dublin was twice interrupted after fans threw tennis balls onto the pitch featuring the Palestinian flag.

The FAI eventually took a vote of its delegates in July, in which 75 members voted to play the matches and 32 voted to boycott.

Not playing the matches could have harmed Irish football in the long-run, the FAI said, amid the possibility of Uefa sanctions for refusing to fulfil the fixtures and the potential loss of millions of euros in income.

As well as curtailing its coverage, RTE will not take advertising or sponsorship income from the matches, saying it will only "meet its contractual obligations" to broadcast the fixtures.

No tickets are being sold to Irish fans for either the 'home' or 'away' matches, with a small allocation available for Israeli fans for the first fixture, which has been the case at multiple previous Israel home games held in Hungary.

Hungary has been deemed a suitable host nation for Israel matches because the two nations enjoy stronger diplomatic ties than those between Israel and many other European nations, and it has been willing to provide the necessary policing and security arrangements for matches to operate smoothly.

The FAI decided in the summer to play its 'home' fixture against Israel at a neutral stadium, citing "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil".

Reports have claimed the FAI was concerned protests could prevent the match from taking place in Dublin.

The FAI gave no official reason for the selection of Backa Topola, but choosing a venue in Serbia - in a town so remote - in theory renders security management easier and reduces the possibility of protest.

In 2025, Serbian foreign minister Marko Duric described Israel as one of Serbia's "closest friends and strategic partners". Serbia has also purchased military equipment, including drones and missiles, from Israel in recent years.

The decision to play in neutral stadiums has not curtailed opposition.

Fans of various Irish clubs have demonstrated against the matches during domestic fixtures in recent weeks, and on Monday more than 160 Irish athletes signed an open letter by the Irish Sport for Palestine group urging a boycott. The signatories include boxer Tyrone McKenna and former European champion athlete Ciara Mageean.

FAI CEO David Courrell said last week Uefa had rejected a request for the teams to be kept apart in future draws, director of football John Martin described the games as a "very uncomfortable situation for everyone". Manager Heimer Hallgrimsson, meanwhile, said playing the match did not constitute legitimisation of Israel's "genocide".

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," Hallgrimmson said. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

In response, the Israel Football Association accused Hallgrimsson of "ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity".

The Republic of Ireland faced Israel in Women's EuroBasket qualifiers last autumn and earlier this year after "extensive deliberations".

The Republic of Ireland has been among the European countries to most keenly show support for Palestinians since the start of Israel's military offensive in Gaza in October 2023.

More than 73,000 people have been killed in Israeli attacks, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations (UN).

In May 2024, alongside Spain and Norway, Ireland officially recognised a Palestinian state, and later that year joined South Africa's Gaza genocide case against Israel in the International Court of Justice.

The country has also boycotted Eurovision since 2025 because of Israel's ongoing participation in the song contest, was the first EU country to ban goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, and has issued travel bans for Israeli government ministers.

On Monday, Irish foreign minister Helen McEntee said: "Ireland's view is clear - international law is being breached. We are seeing an attempt to erase a population."

Israel has criticised Ireland's standpoint and claims its actions in Gaza constitute self-defence, after the armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.

Last summer a UN commission of inquiry found that Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, and this year a further investigation determined that the country has deliberately targeted children with military force, resulting in genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

Israel has repeatedly rejected allegations it has committed genocide.

The Republic of Ireland is not the only nation to have expressed reluctance to face Israel in international football.

In 2024, Belgium refused to host Israel on home soil, and the match was held instead in Debrecen.

The president of the Norwegian Football Association, Lise Klaveness, made a public statement last year saying Israel should be suspended from European competitions, and Turkey also called for Israel to be banned.

In a statement released on Tuesday, Amnesty International said Uefa was "giving Israel an international stage" rather than "sending a clear message there is a cost" for its actions in Gaza.

BBC Sport reported last autumn that Uefa executives were considering a vote on whether to ban Israel, under pressure from representatives from a number of nations.

But any plan to hold a vote was pulled when the first phase of a ceasefire was announced last October.

title: GB out of BJK Cup as Kartal & Boulter beaten by Czechs
description: Sonay Kartal and Katie Boulter lose their singles matches as Great Britain are beaten by a strong Czech Republic side in the Billie Jean King Cup quarter-finals.
fullText:
Sonay Kartal and Katie Boulter lost their respective singles matches as Great Britain were beaten by a strong Czech Republic side in the Billie Jean King Cup quarter-finals.

Anne Keothavong's team headed into the tie as underdogs, with all five Czech players placed higher in the singles rankings than any of the British squad.

Sonay Kartal produced a gritty performance as she returned to tennis after six months out with a lower back injury, but fell to a narrow 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 6-4 defeat in a marathon three-hour encounter with Marie Bouzkova.

Boulter could do little to get Britain back into the best-of-three tie as she was outplayed 6-2 7-6 (7-3) by Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

It was a second successive loss for Boulter at the hands of a Czech player, coming just three weeks after a 58-minute demolition by Karolina Muchova at the US Open.

It is the first time since 2023 that Britain have failed to reach the semi-finals at the Billie Jean King Cup and their wait for a maiden title will go on for another year.

The Czech Republic, who are 11-time winners of the tournament and the only team boasting two top-10 players at the Finals, will face either Kazakhstan or Spain in Friday's semi-finals.

Playing her first match since retiring injured in the fourth round at Indian Wells in March, Kartal started well and struck early against world number 26 Bouzkova.

However, she was broken back immediately and Bouzkova dominated the tie-break to take the opener.

The Briton broke early in the second set and held on to force a decider, but her first double fault of the match handed Bouzkova a break for a 4-2 lead.

Kartal delayed defeat by saving three match points and breaking back, but Bouzkova restored her lead immediately to clinch victory after exactly three hours on court to put the Czechs in front.

With Noskova and Muchova - this year's Wimbledon finalists - in the Czech squad, it was always going to be a uphill battle for number one Boulter.

Two double faults in the first game saw Boulter drop serve early and world number six Noskova steamrolled her way through the opening four games before wrapping up the set.

Boulter improved in the second set and threatened to force a decider, but she was unable to create a single break point and Noskova took control of the tie-break to send her nation into the semi-finals.

title: Arteta agrees new deal with champions Arsenal
description: Mikel Arteta agrees an improved new contract with Premier League champions Arsenal.
fullText:
Mikel Arteta has agreed an improved new contract with Premier League champions Arsenal.

The Spaniard's current deal expires at the end of this season but talks over a new contract have been ongoing for a number of months.

BBC Sport reported earlier this month that an agreement between all parties was close.

And it is now understood Arteta has reached a final agreement with the Gunners to extend his stay.

There is no confirmation over the length of his new contract but it is set to take him into at least his 10th year at the club following his arrival in December 2019.

The new contract will also include a sharp pay increase from his current salary of £10m per year plus an additional £5m in bonuses.

Speaking about his contract talks, Arteta said last week that fans did not need to "worry" because he wanted to stay.

"I'm extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with," he said.

News of Arteta's agreement over a new deal at Arsenal won't come as a shock - but it is a major development nevertheless.

The fact his existing deal expires at the end of the season did put a slightly greater emphasis on the speed of discussions than normal.

But Arteta has been transparent about his desire to stay at the club beyond the end of this campaign.

Dynasty building is what has driven Arteta's decision. Winning Arsenal's first Premier League title in 20 years last season is viewed as just the start.

Coming within a penalty kick of winning their first Champions League trophy came as a gut-wrenching blow - but also a huge motivation.

With that in mind, there was never a sense Arteta was preparing to walk away from the team he has built to become one of the best in European football.

So with a deal for their manager to stay now agreed, the foundation of Arsenal's recent revitalisation into a footballing force remains in place.

Does more history beckon? Arteta is committed to finding out.
