title: Jet Greaves remains calm, cool and collected for Columbus Blue Jackets
description: Columbus Blue Jackets goalie Jet Greaves impresses in preseason debut, unfazed by new deal worth $15 million.
fullText:
Less than a week into Blue Jackets training camp, Jet Greaves is already putting a muzzle on concerns about carrying the weight of increased expectations with a new $5 million salary.

More: Columbus Blue Jackets open preseason with 1-0 win over Detroit Red Wings

Rather than melting under the pressure, the Blue Jackets goalie looks and sounds even calmer than before he boosted his pay rate through a tough summer negotiation that nearly forced Greaves to become the first player in franchise history to need an arbitration hearing.

Instead, a last minute request to delay the hearing led to talks in Toronto that resulted in a deal that will pay him a total of $15 million. That's an increase of roughly $4.2 million per season, but Greaves is handling his new salary and status in stride.

He's been sharp to start training camp, including practice drills, a scrimmage and the first two periods of the Blue Jackets' 1-0 shootout victory over the Detroit Red Wings on Sept. 21at Nationwide Arena to open their four game preseason schedule.

"Of course, some things are different," Greaves said. "I'm fortunate to have a little more experience now, which I think is helping me in how I approach each day, but there's a lot of the same [stuff as before]. Every day I come to the rink, it's about improving, learning and enjoying being at the rink, and I feel like that's been a lot of the same. So, I've really been enjoying it."

That's certainly how it looked against the Red Wings, who failed to beat Greaves on 16 shots in the first two periods and dominated the first by outshooting the Blue Jackets 11-3. Greaves (6-0, 188) stood tall despite being undersized for a goalie.

"You never know what the situation is going to be," Greaves said. "Sometimes you're busy at the start of the game and then it's a little slower later on, or sometimes [it's] vice versa ... but I think in the first game of the preseason, it's maybe nice to see some pucks and get into the game early. Either way, I just enjoy being out there. It's awesome to be back out there with the guys and everything."

Thanks to the NHL's new 84-game schedule and a corresponding reduction in preseason games, Greaves will only get to do that once more time before games start to count. His next start will be Sept. 26 in Detroit, when the Blue Jackets conclude the preseason with a rematch against the Red Wings.

That's not a lot of preparation time for goalies, but Greaves has a level head about that too.

"It's going to be urgent for us to get to our game right away, once the season starts, and the best way to do that is get to it right now," he said. "Whatever the situation is, it's my job to be ready."

Dispatch Blue Jackets/Crew reporter Brian Hedger can be reached at bhedger@dispatch.com

title: J.J. Spaun Wins BMW PGA Championship Urges Americans To Embrace The DP World Tour
description: J.J. Spaun isn’t just playing golf in England; he is making a case for the DP World Tour to become a regular stop for top Americans. His strong run at the BMW PGA Championship proves that playing abroad is not a punishment but a genuine opportunity. The 2025 U.
fullText:
J.J. Spaun isn't just playing golf in England; he is making a case for the DP World Tour to become a regular stop for top Americans. His strong run at the BMW PGA Championship proves that playing abroad is not a punishment but a genuine opportunity. The 2025 U.S. Open champion arrived at Wentworth with a clear plan, and his performance suggests that other Americans should follow his lead.

Spaun's connection to this part of the world runs deeper than just a tournament invite. He and his family actually vacation in the Cotswolds every winter. "My family and I actually vacation over here in the wintertime," Spaun said after the second round. This routine gives him a reason to visit beyond the fairways. Whenever a reason arises to visit the U.K., particularly England, he tries to make it happen. That personal stake changes how he approaches the event. He's a regular guest, not just a visitor.

The trips happen in mid-December, a time when most players are resting. During mid-December, they spend a couple weeks in the Cotswolds simply enjoying the English culture. It's a simple life away from the pressure. This balance is what many players crave but rarely find on the main tour.

Spaun's experience at Wentworth has solidified his plans for the coming season. He isn't looking to leave the PGA Tour entirely, but he sees a new rhythm emerging. "I definitely feel like I'm going to plan a little bit more of a global schedule or a European schedule moving forward in the fall time," Spaun stated. This is a direct message to his peers. If a major champion can thrive here, why not others?

According to Yahoo Sports, these comments arrive at a critical moment for the DP World Tour. The league faces a massive shift as LIV Golf files for bankruptcy, potentially forcing a wave of players to seek new options. Because Spaun is an American with little historical participation on the European circuit, his endorsement carries substantial weight. His victory at the BMW PGA Championship, where he closed at 17 under par, demonstrates the path is open.

The timing is perfect for players like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton, who are already members and will likely serve suspensions on this tour. But for Americans, the hesitation remains. Spaun's voice cuts through that doubt. He has tested the waters and found them warm. "The community is great, the spectators and fans are great," he said. That's a strategic shift in how the game is played, not just polite talk.

Spaun's journey also highlights a personal hurdle he overcame to get here. He finished 10th on the points list for the Presidents Cup but was left off the American roster. "Yeah, I think it was disappointing to be left off," he admitted. That sting likely fueled his drive at Wentworth. He is using this platform to show that the global game is where the future lies. With the DP World Tour looking for new blood and Spaun proving the waters are warm, the door is wide open for more Americans to follow suit this fall.

title: Afghan cyclist who escaped Taliban wins Asian Games medal
description: Fariba Hashimi hoped her silver medal would inspire future generations of athletes to follow their dreams
fullText:
Afghan cyclist Fariba Hashimi, who fled the country after the Taliban's return to power, won a brilliant silver in the women's road race at the Asian Games and said she hoped her success story would inspire others to follow her path.

The 23-year-old had to disguise herself as a man during training for her own safety and was attacked with stones and bottles in her early years in the sport, before escaping Afghanistan alongside her sister, fellow professional cyclist Yulduz, after the Taliban retook control in 2021.

The sisters, from Faryab province in northern Afghanistan, fled to Italy, where they are now based, and competed at the Paris Olympics in 2024.

Fariba, who finished seventh in the women's time trial at the Asian Games, said she hoped her performances would encourage other girls and women living under the repressive Taliban regime to chase their own sporting ambitions.

She said: "I can't explain my feelings now. I was born inside a country where the women who dream are getting attacked, and I'm really happy that I have fought against that.

"I hope that the next generation will come here and represent their country without any fear.

"This silver medal can show a lot of resilience from Afghan women, and I'm really happy. I'm not alone, I know that behind me millions of women, from many countries, have the same dream and they are standing with me."

Hashimi hopes to compete at the LA Olympics in 2028, adding: "I never want to give up and hopefully we can see [what can happen] again in Los Angeles."

She also thanked the Japanese team for their contribution to her silver medal, which she won behind China's Guo Li. Hashimi did not have a mechanic with her at the Games in Nagoya, Japan, and said: "We were fixing the bike ourselves. I was the mechanic for myself. I was washing the bike myself. Thank you to the Japanese team. They were really, really nice to me, fixed my bike."

title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement
description: South Africa's most successful Olympian Tatjana Smith explains why she has reversed her decision to retire from competitive swimming.
fullText:
Having ended a two-year exile from competitive swimming, South Africa's most successful Olympian Tatjana Smith has revealed she "lost the love" for her sport before stepping away from the pool in 2024.

The 29-year-old's decision to retire straight after the Paris Games came as a surprise, given she had just won 200m breaststroke gold in the French capital to add to her 100m title from Tokyo 2020.

But after two years away, which included several months in which she did not swim at all, Smith says she is now "free from the things that made me hate swimming".

"My whole life, I was kind of a robot towards swimming," she told Newsday on the BBC World Service.

"You're so zoned in, you're obsessed with something, so there isn't actually time for you to think about things outside of the pool that you potentially have a passion for.

"I think probably everyone would think that the timing [of retirement] was the worst. But I absolutely 100% believe it was the best decision at that time, and I still have so much peace about it."

Having also picked up a silver medal in both Tokyo and Paris, Smith's total of four Olympic medals for South Africa is matched only by fellow swimmer Chad le Clos, who claimed one gold and three silvers across the London 2012 and Rio 2016 Games.

Smith on retirement and becoming South Africa's most decorated Olympian

But despite making history for her country, Smith says financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, also contributed to her decision to retire.

"The financial burden on any athlete is so tough," she explained.

"I relied on my parents funding me until I broke the world record at the Olympics. And then, all of a sudden, now people are interested in maybe sponsoring you.

"But the majority of sponsorships for athletes are based on performance. So then you have that pressure and expectation to always have to perform, otherwise you're not going to get paid.

"I think the financial side, and also being in a system where they're not really putting the athletes first, made it really difficult."

Smith won her first Olympic title under her maiden name Schoenmaker, before changing her surname when she married sports agent Joel Smith in 2023.

The marriage made her part of a wider South African sporting dynasty, given that her sister-in-law is Rachel Smith, who was married to Springboks captain Siya Kolisi before their split.

Tatjana Smith admits her own marriage changed the way she thought about her future.

"Thinking about families as a woman, you have to time it perfectly, because if you're pregnant, it's not like you can still compete."

While children are not yet part of her journey, Smith says working out what to do next was far from easy.

"I definitely understand what athletes mean from the post-Olympic depression," said the 2023 200m breaststroke world champion, who also counts Commonwealth and African titles among her achievements.

"It was such an emptiness in my life, because my whole life revolved around swimming.

"I don't have to eat at a certain time, I don't have to sleep at a certain time, I don't have to think about travelling or not spending time with family anymore.

"The world is so overwhelming. It's like, in which direction to go?

"It was definitely the toughest season that I had to go through. I think it's probably why it's made me a stronger person."

Initially, Smith took on speaking engagements to pay the bills.

She smiles when she admits: "I hate public speaking. I hate being in front of people."

The same cannot be said of her love for competition.

Having returned to the pool in order to keep fit, she decided to have a crack at triathlon, something she describes as a "crazy idea".

"The training was so intense, and I was like, 'OK, I might as well just go back to swimming if I'm going to train this hard'," she said.

"Every time I went back to the swimming pool and I dived in, I was like, 'Yeah, this is a feeling that I really miss so much'.

"I think slowly over the year and a half, I just realised 'Wow, I really do love swimming'."

Having made her decision to come out of retirement, Smith now wants to freshen things up and "try something new".

That means a change to the 50m breaststroke, an event which has just been added to the Olympic schedule for the first time ahead of the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.

"I thought, 'Why don't I try? Why don't I give myself that challenge? Reinvent myself'," said Smith.

"I always try and describe it to someone that maybe doesn't understand swimming; it's like a 400m runner and a 100m [runner]. It's two different body types, two different trainings, and that's where I'm going."

It means she has more than halved her training volume, with three sessions a week instead of eight - a change she believes will help her retain her love for her sport and live a more balanced life.

"I feel like I'm being so lazy because I used to do 12km per day and now the focus is on taking time to be as explosive as possible.

"Now I'm doing 12km over a whole week.

"I have 20 years of endurance in my pocket, but I can definitely see I don't have those fast twitch [muscle] fibres. It's a whole different way of teaching my body how to swim."

Those initial 20 years in the pool left Smith feeling burned out.

Now she says she has earned the right to do things on her terms.

"Swimming was an opportunity given to me by my parents and I believe I took it on full heartedly.

"But, for the first time, it's my decision whether I want to come back. I'm choosing swimming.

"I've achieved way more than I ever dreamed in my whole life, so I have nothing to prove."

title: ‘It’s humbling’ – Kelsey Mitchell gives her honest verdict on being part of WNBA MVP conversation
description: The race to be crowned the WNBA MVP in 2026 is heating up, and Kelsey Mitchell has now given her verdict on being part of the conversation. Mitchell recently made history when she set a WNBA single-season scoring record by taking her total for 2026 up to 1,034 points during a Fever game last week.
fullText:
The race to be crowned the WNBA MVP in 2026 is heating up, and Kelsey Mitchell has now given her verdict on being part of the conversation.

Mitchell recently made history when she set a WNBA single-season scoring record by taking her total for 2026 up to 1,034 points during a Fever game last week.

Now, Kelsey has been speaking about the 2026 MVP race and admitted she is humbled to be involved.

In a recent video that has been shared on X/Twitter, she said: "I've never talked to S*** magazine before. I've never been a part of the MVP conversation before. All this is kind of like, in a way, gracefully new. It's humbling.

"I don't know how I feel about people kind of like, noticing who I am. But I appreciate the basketball the people can see from me. That's important.

"I wouldn't really say I care about the MVP, who wins it. But I would say I'm glad that this is just about basketball for me.

"As long as we talk about basketball and Kelsey Mitchell, that's all I kind of want to keep it about.

"There's so many great players in this league, whoever wins it deserves it."

Alongside Mitchell, fellow Fever star Caitlin Clark is also in the running to be named MVP this season.

However, both Indiana players are competing against multi-time champion A'ja Wilson, who could win the award for a record fifth time.

title: Springboks announce new captain as team to face Australia revealed
description: Andre Esterhuizen will lead the world champions in the clash in Perth
fullText:
Andre Esterhuizen will captain South Africa for the first time in a heavily-changed Springboks team for the one-off Test against Australia in Perth.

The versatile Esterhuizen, who can also play in the back row, skippers the side from the centres as Rassie Erasmus makes 13 alterations to the starting XV that beat New Zealand in the fourth Rugby's Greatest Rivalry clash in Baltimore.

Handre Pollard returns to wear the No 10 shirt having missed out on an appearance in the All Blacks series due to injury, while Eben Etzebeth and Franco Mostert form an experienced second row partnership.

Jasper Wiese is set to win his 50th cap as one of six forwards named on the bench, while Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende have been released from camp having been rested ahead of South Africa's Nations Championship fixtures in November.

"Each player in this squad has been working hard at training over the last few months and have had a chance to play in either the first leg of the Nations Championship or RGR, or both, while guys like Handre and Canan have recovered from injury, and they are all quality players, so we are pleased to give them a run and we are excited to see this team in action," said Erasmus.

"Australia poses a completely different threat to New Zealand in the way they play, so we believe these combinations would be best suited for the challenge that we will face against them."

"[Esterhuizen has] captained the Sharks, and he has brought so much to our squad off and on the field, both at centre and in the loose trio, and he thoroughly deserves this opportunity.

"It will also help build our leadership core even more within the team with several players having captained the side over the last few seasons, and we trust that he is the right man to take over the captaincy in this match."

The Springboks fought back from 1-0 down to beat New Zealand 3-1 in the landmark new series that formed the centrepiece of a busy international year.

Erasmus's side will enjoy more than a month off before resuming their Nations Championship campaign against Italy on 7 November, with clashes to come against France and Ireland.

title: Sean McVay seemingly takes blame for LA Rams playing their Week 1 game in Australia
description: Following their win against the New York Giants, LA Rams head coach Sean McVay made a joke about their difficult trip down under for their season opener. The Rams earned their first win of the season against the New York Giants, beating John Harbaugh’s side in a 28-6 blowout.
fullText:
Following their win against the New York Giants, LA Rams head coach Sean McVay made a joke about their difficult trip down under for their season opener.

The Rams earned their first win of the season against the New York Giants, beating John Harbaugh's side in a 28-6 blowout.

However, even with this return to winning ways, head coach Sean McVay still can't stop thinking about their loss at Melbourne Cricket Ground.

After the LA Rams' win against the New York Giants, Sean McVay spoke to reporters about the team's performance following a loss in Week 1.

McVay joked that losses can be lessons for the team, and suggested that he made a mistake as a coach by letting the team play their first game overseas.

"Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn. And sometimes you have a d—— coach that makes travel plans that puts you in bad spots."

Even though McVay was joking, one has to imagine that the Rams head coach had to give the green light for the Rams to play in Australia when the plans were being made.

The Week 1 fixture in Australia came as part of the NFL's global expansion plan, as the league tries to attract a bigger international audience.

Over the last few years, the NFL has held games in Brazil, England, Germany, and Australia, while boasting massive attendance figures.

But with these games moving abroad, players are forced to take long flights to different time zones. As a result, they have to take a great toll on their bodies beyond the pain they endure on the gridiron.

After their loss to the San Francisco 49ers in their opening fixture, McVay claimed that the Rams had suffered greatly because of the long travel hours.

The Rams had to travel 17 hours to reach Melbourne, and only arrived in the city 24 hours before their game, giving them almost no time to decompress physically.

Whereas the 49ers had arrived in Australia two days prior, giving them a chance to adapt to the time zone and have some practice sessions in the Australian weather.

Hopefully, McVay can continue this momentum and get the team to go on a string of wins as the season goes on.

description: Kentucky returns home as heavy favorites against a 2-1 South Alabama team that are trying to pull off an upset.
fullText:
Kentucky Football is coming off its biggest win of the season, defeating No. 9 Texas A&M, 31-21, on the road. The Wildcats dominated the second half, outscoring the Aggies 24-14 while scoring multiple touchdowns and forcing turnovers.

The victory marked the first major road win of Will Stein's tenure and improved Kentucky to 2-1 overall and 1-1 in SEC play.

Now, Kentucky gets a more favorable matchup in Week 4 against South Alabama at Kroger Field. The Wildcats will look to improve to 3-1 before traveling to face South Carolina.

South Alabama enters the matchup at 2-1 after defeating Southeastern Louisiana 39-14 and Ohio 41-36, while falling short to Tulane 28-24. Quarterback Bishop Davenport started the Jaguars' first two games before missing the Ohio game with a minor injury. Jared Hollins stepped in and threw for 192 yards and a touchdown in the victory.

Davenport has completed 40/59 passes for 450 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions this season.

South Alabama also relies on its running back room featuring Keenan Phillips, P.J. Martin and Trae'von Dunbar, while Brendan Jenkins and Micah Woods are among the team's primary receiving options.

Kentucky also has some familiarity with South Alabama, having added defensive linemen Dominic Wiseman and Tyler Thomas from the Jaguars.

title: Ja’Marr Chase says defense is the Bengals’ ‘backbone’ this season
description: The revamped defense continues impressive start.
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bengals made it clear this offseason that they were all in on revamping a roster that missed the postseason three years in a row.

The Bengals brought in so many decorated veterans like Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe, and Bryan Cook to create a new culture and create it as quickly as possible.

Through the first two weeks of play, that investment is showing, and it's showing as quickly as the front office had hoped.

The Bengals defense dominated both the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Houston Texans, which has stunned the NFL world.

After a two-touchdown day this past weekend, Ja'Marr Chase shared his thoughts on the defense so far and gave that unit some major props.

"I can't even describe how much I love our defense right now," Chase stated. "They're our backbone. We're going to feed off their energy."

Chase has never shied away from speaking his truth to the media, and he showed love for a unit that has not complemented the Bengals offense the past few years.

The Bengals are officially 2-0 to start a season in the Burrow-Taylor era with Joe Burrow healthy going into week 3.

#Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase on his team’s new-look defense: “I can’t even describe how much I love our defense right now. They’re our backbone and we’re going to feed off their energy.”

title: Jose Mourinho will not attend coaches’ meeting amid Real Madrid refereeing tensions
description: It has only been around a month since the start of the 2026-27 season, but Real Madrid have already been left with several refereeing-related grievances. The Merengues had already been protesting some...
fullText:
It has only been around a month since the start of the 2026-27 season, but Real Madrid have already been left with several refereeing-related grievances. The Merengues had already been protesting some of the refereeing decisions in earlier games, but matters came to a head during the Madrid derby.

This match saw the referee, Ortiz Arias, being embroiled in several controversies, including a red card for Dean Huijsen, two possible red cards not shown to Atletico Madrid players Cuti Romero and Kang-In Lee, and another handball by Marc Pubill inside the Atletico penalty box that was not called for a penalty.

The drama surrounding the referees continued after the match, as Jose Mourinho very harshly criticized the federation and the officials for the game. In such a context, a coaches' meeting was scheduled to take place today, on Tuesday.

In recent years, this annual meeting has served as a platform where coaches from the top two divisions in Spain gather and talk about some of their problems, especially related to finances and refereeing.

However, as Diario AS has reported, Mourinho will not be attending this meeting, and has already explained his reasons for this. Usually, these meetings are well attended, with coaches from the big three clubs in Spain, Real Madrid, FC Barcelona, and Atletico Madrid also frequently in attendance. Diego Simeone has rarely missed any of these meetings, but this time, his presence is also doubtful because of personal reasons, but Hansi Flick will be in attendance.

With the way Real Madrid and referees have once again ended up in quite an open and public conflict, this matter will have to be addressed by the relevant authorities as soon as possible. The integrity of one of the very top leagues in Europe is at stake, and CTA, RFEF, and La Liga will have to ensure the reservations of all the relevant stakeholders are addressed to avoid this problem from further escalating.

title: ‘Hate to see that’ – Peyton and Eli Manning left stunned by Jaxson Dart injury during Giants-Rams
description: New York Giants fans feared the worst when Jaxson Dart went down in the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams. Dart took a big hit after throwing a perfect pass to tight end Theo Johnson.
fullText:
New York Giants fans feared the worst when Jaxson Dart went down in the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams. Dart took a big hit after throwing a perfect pass to tight end Theo Johnson.

The Giants quarterback was visibly hurt and exited the field with a knee injury. While many assumed it would be a long-term issue, Dart has reportedly suffered a sprained MCL and could return before the end of October.

Peyton Manning and his brother Eli, who won two Super Bowls with the Giants, were both concerned about Dart after watching the incident. They will be relieved that the 23-year-old has not suffered a major injury, but it could still derail the Giants' season.

Jaxson Dart impressed in the New York Giants' Week 1 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. He threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns in one of last weekend's best quarterback performances.

The new-look Giants, led by head coach John Harbaugh, entered their Week 2 clash with the Los Angeles Rams full of confidence. However, their bubble burst almost immediately when Dart exited the game in the first quarter.

We now understand the Giants' season is not over, as Dart is likely to return within two months. But Peyton and Eli Manning did not know that when Dart was lying on the floor after taking a hit from Rams defender Byron Young.

Peyton reacted on ESPN's ManningCast: "Oh no. Oh no. No. No. No. No. That is not what we want to see. Gosh. Ugh, come on." Eli added: "Tough to watch. Hate to see that. Hopefully he's okay."

Of course, everyone wants Dart to return for his own sake, but it also matters a great deal to the Giants. They only scored six points with Jameis Winston under centre, suggesting they may not win many games in Dart's absence.

title: “When Jürgen Klopp calls, you can’t say no” – Eintracht Frankfurt forward on choosing Germany over Morocco
description: Jürgen Klopp has included several new faces in his extended 44-man squad for Germany’s four upcoming UEFA Nations League matches.One of them is Younes Ebnoutalib, who was convinced to choose German...
fullText:
Jürgen Klopp has included several new faces in his extended 44-man squad for Germany's four upcoming UEFA Nations League matches.

One of them is Younes Ebnoutalib, who was convinced to choose Germany over Morocco after receiving a call from the 59-year-old former Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool coach.

"There were talks with Morocco. But when Jürgen Klopp calls, you can't say no," Ebnoutalib told German media on Tuesday.

Klopp gave his first speech to the players on Monday and has left striker with a strong first impression.

"The impression is very positive. He is, of course, someone who brings a great deal of experience and already has a certain presence because of what he has achieved over the years. So, naturally, you have a great deal of respect for him. But he was very nice and very likeable in the conversations," Ebnoutalib said, according to Bild.

"He is already very well known for the way he wants to play football. With high pressing, with a lot of energy and power. He has already fired us up. I think that's what he is known for, that he is very good at reaching people and getting them on board. He has certainly got us in the right mindset."

The 23-year-old will be hoping to make his Germany debut against the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Thursday.

title: ‘I am very sorry…’: Man Utd star speaks out after MEN journo confirms growing ‘tension’ behind the scenes
description: Benjamin Sesko has spoken directly to Slovenia fans to confirm that he will be unavailable for the team’s upcoming fixtures.The Manchester United forward is said to have suffered a re-aggravation of...
fullText:
Benjamin Sesko has spoken directly to Slovenia fans to confirm that he will be unavailable for the team's upcoming fixtures.

The Manchester United forward is said to have suffered a re-aggravation of the shin injury that was causing him problems throughout his maiden campaign at Old Trafford.

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Sesko took to Instagram this morning to address the speculation over his rumoured absence, saying: "I am very sorry that I will have to miss the national team's upcoming matches.

"I have always played for Slovenia – and always will – with heart and pride. Right now, the most important thing is to focus fully on my recovery. I am already working on getting back on the pitch as soon as possible to help both the national team and my club once again.

"I believe in our guys, and I am convinced that this time, too, they will display the team spirit that has always defined us. I can't wait to wear the national team jersey again; until then, I will be Slovenia's biggest fan. Go Slovenia!"

Meanwhile, Manchester Evening News journalist Tyrone Marshall revealed on Monday that there has been growing 'tension' between United and the Slovenia team regarding the striker's fitness.

Sesko has not featured for his nation in 11 months, and that streak will now be extended until at least mid-November.

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Of course, United's priority is ensuring he's fit for when they resume their action after the three-week break.

The 23-year-old missed out against Fulham on Sunday after pulling up with some pain following the midweek defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sesko is still awaiting his first Premier League start of the term, despite being the only out-and-out No.9 in Michael Carrick's ranks.

The manager has preferred to utilise Matheus Cunha up front, with the Brazilian scoring his first goal of the campaign over the weekend to rescue a point at Craven Cottage.

title: The controversial moment that helped India avoid embarrassing cricket upset to Japan
description: India escaped with a narrow two-run win over Japan ahead of their Asian Games title defence
fullText:
India escaped with a narrow two-run win over Japan to avoid one of the greatest upsets in cricket history in their shortened T20 match at Sano.

The game was reduced to five overs due to rain and India struggled on the placid pitch after electing to bat first, with skipper Shreyas Iyer producing a top-score of 16 off 12 balls alongside Sanju Samson's nine.

Charlie Hara-Hinze claimed two wickets for 17 runs as India finished on 32 for four and the hosts were pegged back in their chase with Lachlan Yamamoto-Lake and Ibrahim Takahashi falling in the opening two overs.

Captain Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming led the response for Japan with 12 before being dismissed by Washington Sundar and Benjamin Ito-Davis added nine as India scraped to victory.

There was a dramatic moment in the final over when India were frustrated about a wide signalled by the umpire and following a discussion with the square leg umpire, the decision was overturned.

"Honestly speaking, it was a very difficult wicket to bat on," Iyer said after the match. "A five-over game, it can go anywhere. It doesn't matter how good a team you are.

"The attitude and approach ​the ⁠Japanese team showed today was impeccable, and ‌kudos to them. Their approach was outstanding. I'm sure that they are on the right track."

Kadowaki-Fleming said he was extremely proud of ⁠his team's performance against such formidable opposition.

"Emotions are running pretty high in our group. But the fact that we're able to run the best team in the world, in my opinion, to the last ball of a game is pretty special," he said.

"I think today was a really momentous occasion in that it was the first time we were able to face a full member."

Minnows Japan had used diplomatic channels to line up the high-profile match against India.

India agreed to the meeting partly on the basis that they could use the game to get used to conditions in Japan before beginning their Asian Games title defence.

India could yet face Japan in their Asian Games opener as they prepare to begin their campaign at the quarter-final stage, bypassing the group alongside Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Bangladesh because of their seeding.

They will be pitted against the runner-up of Group A, which consists of Afghanistan, Japan and Nepal, on Monday 28 September at Korogi Sports Park, Nisshin.

title: OKC Comets vs Las Vegas Aviators in PCL Championship Series, what to know, how to watch
description: OKC opens the PCL Championship Series at Las Vegas on Tuesday, aiming to advance to the Triple-A championship for the second time since 2023.
fullText:
The Oklahoma City Comets have a chance to win big in Sin City.

OKC opens the PCL Championship Series at Las Vegas on Tuesday, aiming to advance to the Triple-A championship for the second time since 2023. First pitch of Game 1 in the best-of-three series is at 9:05 p.m. CT.

The Comets finished 48-27 in the second half of the season to advance, including an 18-3 record over the final 21 games. They were 89-60 overall, the top record in the PCL and one game shy of the top mark in Triple A.

The Aviators, the affiliate of the Athletics, finished 87-61 overall, 1.5 games behind the Comets in the overall standings. But they won the first-half PCL title to advance and host the playoffs.

More: MLB power rankings: Remember the Rangers? Texas has playoff bid in reach

When: 9:05 p.m. CT Tuesday-Thursday

Where: Las Vegas Ballpark in Las Vegas

Streaming: MLB+, Bally Sports Live; Games 1 & 2 free on MLB.com and MiLB.com for registered users

More: These MLB sluggers are chasing an ugly record. Will history be made this week?

The Comets were 6.5 games behind Sugar Land for first place on Aug. 21.

OKC rattled off 21 wins in 27 games to close out the season and win the Pacific Coast League East crown by six games over Sugar Land. OKC won 14 straight games at one point.

This is the fifth time the franchise has made the postseason since its affiliation with the Los Angeles Dodgers began in 2015. OKC won the PCL championship in 2023, a first in the Bricktown era.

OKC also made the PCL Championship Series during the Bricktown era in 1999, 2008 and 2016.

More: How do MLB playoffs work? Tiebreakers, format, matchups explained

The trio of James Tibbs III, Ryan Fitzgerald and Zach Ehrhard have been with the Comets all season, and they've put up big numbers.

Tibbs has 30 homers and is one of two players in the league to reach the milestone this season. Tibbs is also the seventh player in the Bricktown era to hit 30 or more homers in a season, with his 107 RBIs ranking second in the era and second in the PCL this season. Tibbs also has a Bricktown-era record 108 walks.

Tibbs, the Dodgers' No. 7-ranked prospect, is the first PCL player to have 100 or more RBIs, runs and walks in a season since Albuquerque's Greg Brock in 1982.

Fitzgerald has 172 hits this season, which leads Minor League Baseball and is a Bricktown-era record.

Ehrhard, a former Oklahoma State star who is the organization's 15th-best prospect, led the PCL with 120 runs, also a Bricktown-era record. His 155 hits only trail Fitzgerald in the PCL.

More: One fatal flaw on each MLB contender that could derail long playoff run

Don't overlook the prospect star power for OKC.

The Comets have Jackson Ferris, a 6-foot-4 left-handed pitcher who could be the Game 1 starter. He took a perfect game deep into his last outing. He finished the regular season strong, allowing just four runs in 36 innings with 48 strikeouts, which topped all minor league pitchers.

Outfielder Mike Sirota was also recently promoted to OKC. The second-ranked prospect in the organization, according to MLB Pipeline, climbed from Class A this season.

He led all of MiLB with a .459 on-base percentage and at one point had a 72-game on-base streak.

title: Emile Heskey on the reality of raising professional footballers: ‘It’s not my career, it’s theirs’
description: INTERVIEW: Former England striker Heskey has raised not one but two sons to professional level and speaks to Will Castle about what he got right as a footballer’s parent
fullText:
It's not particularly rare to see the offspring of an ex-professional follow in their parent's footsteps. Usually, though, it's just the one son or daughter that makes it. Two is quite the more remarkable.

Emile Heskey has managed to raise a pair of prodigies through the infamously perilous English academy system. His two sons, Jaden and Reigan, are professional footballers contracted to Manchester City. Eldest Jaden, 20, is on his second loan spell of the year at Sheffield Wednesday, while younger brother Reigan, 18, became the latest City starlet to make tried-and-tested venture to Germany this summer for his maiden loan away, joining Koln. Jadon Sancho, Jamie Gittens and Felix Nmecha are among those to tread the same path to great success, though City will be comforted by the knowledge that if Reigan experiences similar fortunes this term, they'll have him back next June.

Parenting footballers has become a topic of discussion over the past week, thanks to the media swirl surrounding 15-year-old Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel. Frankly, there has already been far too much coverage on what is the future of a child, while the focus on his father's allegedly difficult behaviour has gained significant traction despite the claims mostly being either social media hearsay or from reports citing unverified sources. The point of this piece is not to put more of a spotlight on either individual nor the rumours engulfing them.

What's conclusive, however, is Heskey's triumph in this field. He knows how to nurture the next generation.

Asked if football was always the dream for his sons, he tells The Independent: "I think so - you'd have to ask them!

"From a young age, Jaden wanted to play football. We took him aged three or four, and he just loved it. He loved going to the games. He loved the atmosphere. He loved everything about it. So then he was just programming himself to be the professional footballer that he wants to be.

"Reigan kind of just came along because he's the younger brother. But they've both been talented and they were lucky enough to go to an academy that helped with their progression, helped with their structure, helped with everything to make them the best possible players they could be. I think they were destined to do that."

Former England international Heskey, who turned out for the likes of Liverpool, Leicester and Aston Villa across a 22-year career, admits that his status as an ex-pro gave both his sons a foot in the door.

"100 per cent, there's no doubt that would help. That would give you, let's say, the upper hand," he says. From then, however, it's a level playing field.

"Then you've got to produce something, then you've got to really learn. And that was one of the good things about Jaden, he learns very, very quickly. He's very attentive to what the coaches are talking about. And like I said, Man City had some fantastic coaches."

The right type of coach is integral to an early rise. "This is where it all starts, when you're young - if you get a bad impression from them, it goes sour sometimes," asserts Heskey, who has joined forces with the Chase coaching programme to try and inspire more into the profession. But just as important is the right type of parent.

Heskey says he never tried to be overbearing despite the obvious value of his playing experience. He also didn't let his own motivations take over: "That was easy - for me."

Instead, Heskey's approach was to keep his distance from the whole process. He didn't plaster them on his Instagram with nearly 100,000 followers, he didn't try and build their 'brand' while they were still in primary school.

"I always stood back," he said. "I never stood on the edge so my kids were looking over at me and thought I was overlooking them and scrutinising everything they did. I took a stance back, so that they never saw me - they weren't looking over so they could actually concentrate on the coaches' principles.

"It could be daunting for kids having their parents telling them certain things to do, but then the coach is telling them something else, so there's two different things that they've got going on.

"Sometimes you're best to take a step back because the reality is it's not my career, it's theirs."

Heskey has come across parents that are guilty of the opposite.

"When you look at pushy parents, who is it for? Is it for them or it it for the child?" he questions. "Because I don't think it's for the child, especially some of the times where [you hear] the way the parents talk to them.

"I generally wouldn't talk to my kids [about football] after training because I'd just let them do what they're doing. They're kids."

It got to a point when, during middle adolescence, Heskey had to turn up the intensity and start "grilling" his sons about their impending careers. This, however, led to something of a reality check for the 48-year-old former bagsman.

"I found out that they actually knew more than me," he admits, "because they'd been in an environment which taught them. I would actually be asking them certain things to try and pick their brain, because I was coaching then as well."

With both Jaden and Reigan now navigating the senior game, Heskey's 'less is more' formula holds weight on its own. But those who know the game best tend to agree with the approach. His ex-Liverpool team-mate Jamie Carragher, whose son James plays for Wigan Athletic, has also previously spoken about the damage "nightmare" parents can do to players with promise.

It turns out all you really need is faith, as Heskey finishes: "They're going to be big anyway, so just allow them to grow organically."

title: Rutgers basketball GM Rob Sullivan on how 2026-27 roster came together
description: Q&A with Rutgers basketball general manager Rob Sullivan on how his first offseason went, assembling the 2026-27 roster, and a changing NCAA landscape
fullText:
Rob Sullivan's first offseason as Rutgers basketball's general manager ended with a full and interesting roster – the Scarlet Knights retained most of their top players from last season and added five transfers, three internationals and one traditional freshman. As the 2026-27 season gets underway with full-scale practices, Sullivan shared some insights about the roster-building process and philosophy in a wide-ranging interview.

Q. You were hired last fall. What did you do between November and March that prepared you for the spring's free-agency period?

A. "I'm the connector. It starts with Coach (Steve) Pikiell's vision, and I do whatever it takes to execute that vision. Could be portal intelligence, NIL conversations, agent relationships."

Q. I know you weren't here the offseason before, when they were picking change out of the couch cushions to field a roster, but what would you say about the resources you had for this year's roster?

A. "It starts with Keli (Zinn), who's been awesome. Super intelligent, open-minded, innovative. Keli has provided us with the financial resources to attract the level of talent that will help us win games and compete at the Big Ten level."

Q. You kept most of your top players from last season. What was the retention process like?

A. "That process for me was all last year. I was at almost every practice. I traveled to away games. This was very intentional – I was assessing and evaluating our roster. It ultimately goes back to Coch Pikiell and what his priorities are, but once the season concluded we knew what players we were prioritizing to bring back, and then it goes back to the business side – we knew we had the financial resources to execute that."

Q. We all knew center was going to be a priority in the transfer portal. How did you find and pursue Christian Gurdak?

A. "We're all basketball fans, and throughout the whole year we're canvassing the players that are hooping. I was familiar with Christian based on the great game he had (for Virginia Tech) against Virginia, where he had 19 rebounds and set the ACC freshman record. I also have a familiarity and a relationship with his agent, so that sparked some mutual interest when Christian entered the portal. We wanted to emphasize size in our frontcourt but also a skill set, and he had those pieces."

Q. How about Will Sydnor, Darin Smith and Rasheed Jones? Was there an overriding philosophy in pursuing these transfers?

A. "Yes. We wanted to emphasize size, style of play – do they fit out scheme? – and shooting. When you talk about those guys, they checked a lot of those boxes. I'm very pleased and satisfied with how our roster shook out."

Q. How did you find these international guys?

A. "With the international players, it's about the relationships with agents and every agency we had dealings with. Our rule of thumb is we have to see the guys in person. They have to be assessed and evaluated in person by a member of our Rutgers staff. We felt we had the financial resources to get them. All of these guys played either international competition with their host countries or had professional experience with clubs."

Q. Will you continue to cultivate this market in future offseasons?

A. "It's a great market because they have incredible feel for the game. The top tier of the NBA has a very strong international influence, and that will continue to trickle down collegiately. The NCAA is welcoming and accommodating to international prospects. What we learned in real time is that the younger players, players that are 18-19 years of age, who just finished their academics and are starting to transition to the college ranks and can come in as freshmen, I do think that will continue to happen. But it will be harder for older, more experienced players who have a ton of professional experience, who are 23, 24, 25 years old, to be a trend in the NCAA (eligibility-wise) moving forward."

Q. How challenging has it been to navigate the legal and regulatory complexities with the NCAA and the court and the eligibility rules constantly in flux? I noticed you stayed away from taking fifth-year guys?

A. "We wanted to be aggressive within the rules. NCAA compliance takes precedent. We had different options that came across our desk that we pushed up the chain of command an talked with Keli about the pros an cons, cost-benefit analysis. We made our decisions based on NCAA rules."

Q. Why did you max out the roster at 15 scholarship players?

A. "We wanted the depth and competition, especially in practice. Again, we were fortunate enough that Keli provided us with the budget so we could go down that route. You can see with how physical the conference is that through a long season guys get banged up. We wanted to have options that could keep us rolling."

Q. What's the value in continuing to recruit high school, which is obviously something you remain interested in (Rutgers just got two four-star class of 2027 commitments)?

A. "On our roster we have three players who are exhausting their eligibility. As we approach those scholarship we said, can we backfill those spots this way? I think freshmen are always going to be part of college basketball. Our approach is we expect them to be able to compete right away. We expect them to possibly be in our rotation. And once they get here on campus, they have the full, holistic student-athlete experience and we feel comfortable that we'll be able to retain them for continued development and help them chase their dreams. These guys want to be pros, and we can be a springboard for that, as has ben evident with Ace (Bailey) and Dylan (Harper). So for us, high school recruiting will always be a part of our roster."

Q. What do you think of the Protect College Sports Act?

A. "In my opinion it's a step in the right direction. The hardest thing we're all dealing with right now in college sports is: There needs to be a set of rules that makes it a level playing field. I do think the PCSA will be a step to formulating a set of rules and criteria which will be beneficial."

Q. If the Act becomes law and undergrads are limited to one transfer without penalty, how much does that up the value of bringing in freshmen for example?

A. "As it relates to the transfer rule, that might be something hard to hold up (from legal challenges), but I think you would have guys choosing schools in a more traditional fashion – culture, fit, playing time, ability to improve and chase my dreams, a college diploma. I do think that's been slightly lost with this transitory nature of the unlimited transfer rule. For those of us on the team side it would probably change our recruiting – the program would really know the player and the player would really know the program, and hopefully stay at the institution and get his college diploma, which I think is the goal for all of us."

Q. On the homefront, how is the staff is handling things with Steve undergoing cancer treatment?

A. "We have Pikes' back and he has our full support – his health is our top priority. He was around all summer, at a majority of the summer workouts. When he needs to step away or take time away with his treatment, it's our role to step up and fill the void. From a standpoint of how he's doing, I think he's doing great. He's been around us as everyone has seen, he's a competitor, and he's doing everything he can to be with us throughout the season."

Q. As a Philly guy in Rutgers country, have you found a good cheese steak in Central Jersey yet?

A. "My guy Doug Schneider has the best cheese steak in Central Jersey, DeeDee's (DeeDee's Pizza in Highland Park). He's an incredible Rutgers supporter and it's a fantastic spot."

Jerry Carino has covered the New Jersey sports scene since 1996 and the college basketball beat since 2003. Contact him at jcarino@gannettnj.com.

title: Nebraska lands commitment from class of 2027 forward Dawson Battie
description: Nebraska basketball picked up its second commitment of the 2027 class in four-star power forward Dawson Battie.
fullText:
Nebraska basketball landed a commitment on Monday night from 2027  four-star power forward Dawson Battie. The announcement was made on social media.

Battie is the 27th overall player in the 2027 class, the third overall power forward, and the third overall player in his class from the state of Texas, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings. He drew interest from SMU, Stanford, and Kentucky but ultimately chose Nebraska.

He visited Lincoln three times and recently came to town on September 19. Battie measures in at six-foot-eight, 215 pounds.

Battie has many strengths in his game. He can score at a high level, while also providing rebounding and strong switching on defense. He should fit well in Fred Hoiberg's system because he can create mismatches and pass the ball.

His legs should be an asset on the defensive end of the floor. This is the second commitment for the Huskers in the 2028 recruiting class with small forward Ty Schlagel is the other.

The program has been on a roll lately, and Hoiberg is known for identifying and developing elite talent. This looks like another strong get for the program as they look to contend in the Big Ten for the foreseeable future.

title: Inter’s Calhanoglu Recovery Shows Encouraging Signs Ahead of Parma
description: Hakan Calhanoglu is working individually in the gym as he pushes to be available for Inter’s meeting with Parma, though Chivu is in no rush to throw his regista back into action.According to Gazzett...
fullText:
Hakan Calhanoglu is working individually in the gym as he pushes to be available for Inter's meeting with Parma, though Chivu is in no rush to throw his regista back into action.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport via TuttoMercatoWeb, the Turkish midfielder trained on his own again the day before the report, continuing his recovery from an adductor problem that has become a familiar frustration for both player and club.

Calhanoglu has long been Inter's metronome in midfield, the man who dictates tempo, drives the build-up and still chips in from range or the penalty spot. But the last two seasons have been pockmarked by muscular setbacks that have forced successive coaches, Chivu included, to do without him in some of the biggest fixtures on the calendar.

Calhanoglu himself is keen to be involved against Parma, but Chivu is urging caution to avoid a relapse, which has previously kept him out for longer periods. That caution is rooted in recent history, with the same adductor concern having already ruled him out of the win over Roma.

Per the report, the signals from his individual work are encouraging, but it remains too early to put a firm number on his recovery timeline. Parma, then, is a target rather than a certainty, and Inter's approach to managing his fitness dovetails with the broader caution Chivu has shown in recent team selections around returning players.

title: Henry Pollock signs Northampton Saints contract extension to end speculation over future
description: The 21-year-old has agreed a ‘multi-year’ contract with the Prem champions
fullText:
Henry Pollock has signed a bumper contract extension with Northampton Saints worth more than £400,000 a year to continue his stay with the Prem champions and end the speculation over his future.

The 21-year-old, who has won 13 England caps, was out of contract next summer, with his advisor Eddie Hearn publically seeking a significant pay rise from his previous deal of £150,000 to remain at the Saints.

Pollock signed with Hearn's Matchroom agency in March, with the boxing promoter talking up the back-row forward as a "seven-figure player" and worth £1m a year, although Hearn was not involved in the contract negotiations.

Northampton were always confident of keeping Pollock, despite the noise surrounding his future, and confirmed that a "multi-year" extension had been reached ahead of the start of the new Prem season on Friday.

"I'm massively happy to re-sign with Saints, my boyhood club," Pollock said. "It's an exciting place to be right now. We're in a great spot as a team, but it feels like there's still so much more growth in us.

"I'm still young, and we've got a young squad with a brilliant group of lads. Some of my best mates are here, and every day everyone pushes each other to improve and be the best players and team we can be. For where I am in my career, this is exactly where I want to be."

Pollock started his career with Northampton, making his debut as a 17-year-old schoolboy in 2022, but said during contract negotiations that he was "open to every opportunity" and hinted that he hopes to play abroad in the future.

With fellow England internationals Tommy Freeman, Fin Smith and Alex Mitchell all signing multi-year contract extensions with Northampton in the past 12 months, Pollock set his sights on challenging for the Champions Cup this season as well as defending Northampton's Prem title.

"I feel like we're only just getting started," he said. "We won the Prem last season and we want to go again. Winning the Champions Cup is another huge ambition for us. We came so close a couple of years ago, and achieving that together would be incredibly special."

Northampton's director of rugby Phil Dowson said Pollock still has room to improve but praised the 21-year-old's impact off the pitch in attracting new fans as well as his importance to the Saints on the field.

"We're delighted that Henry has committed his future to Saints," he said. Over the last few years, everyone has seen the quality he brings on the pitch and the speed of his rise through the game – but just as importantly, he's a young man of outstanding character.

"Keeping someone with both his talent and mindset is hugely important for the club. What's most exciting is that there's still so much more to come from him. Henry is incredibly ambitious and constantly looking for ways to improve.

"He's become an important figure not just for Saints, but for the wider game. He inspires young supporters, brings excitement to rugby, and understands that everything off the pitch is built on performing consistently on it. We're excited to see what he can achieve over the coming years."

Northampton confirmed Freeman's re-signing earlier this week, with the England back receiving an uplift in salary.

Prop Emmanuel Iyogun, who has attracted significant interest from elsewhere, and scrum half Archie McParland are among the club's other players out of contract at the end of the campaign, and the club have conceded that they may again not be able to keep everyone they wish to having seen club captain George Furbank depart for Harlequins.

title: “Mwana Mboka” – Ezechiel Banzuzi set for first DR Congo appearance
description: “Mwana Mboka” – meaning “child of the country”. Those were the words Ezechiel Banzuzi used on social media to announce his decision. Our midfielder will now represent DR Congo, the country h...
fullText:
"Mwana Mboka" – meaning "child of the country". Those were the words Ezechiel Banzuzi used on social media to announce his decision. Our midfielder will now represent DR Congo, the country his family comes from, and has now been included in the senior squad for the first time.

The congratulations quickly came flooding in. Castello Lukeba, Ridle Baku, Brajan Gruda and Benjamin Henrichs all reacted to his Instagram post, as did former teammate Xavi Simons.

For the 21-year-old, however, the story behind his decision began much earlier.

"I spoke and thought about it a lot with my family. I'd actually already decided to play for Congo before the World Cup," explained Banzuzi.

Ezechiel was born in the Netherlands and represented the country at various youth levels. But his connection to his family's homeland has always remained strong.

"My family were really happy. They wanted me to play for Congo too and helped me make the decision."

DR Congo's World Cup campaign also reinforced his decision. The Leopards reached the knockout stages for the first time before narrowly losing 2-1 to England in the round of 32.

"I was impressed by how far they got. That definitely played a part in my decision as well. But I already knew before then that there was a lot of potential in this team."

Ezechiel summed up what the decision means to him in two words: "Mwana Mboka".

"It means that you come from that country and you don't forget where you come from. That means a lot to me."

Ezechiel received his first call-up to the DR Congo U23s back in March, although he initially continued to play for the Netherlands U21s. He has now been included in a Congolese senior squad for the first time.

Our midfielder has already spoken to national team head coach Sébastien Desabre on the phone and is now looking forward to his first few days with the Leopards.

"I was really happy to receive my first senior call-up. Now I want to bring my experience to the team and help however I can."

Two important games await Ezechiel on his first senior call-up. DR Congo host Equatorial Guinea on 24th September before travelling to face Zimbabwe on 28th September.

Both matches are qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. The tournament will take place in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19th June to 17th July 2027.

title: La Liga boss: Mourinho living in another galaxy with ref error claims
description: La Liga president Javier Tebas says claiming referees are directed against Real Madrid is “living in another galaxy” as the fallout continued from José Mourinho blaming officials for making key errors in their 2-1 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Sunday. At the post-match press conference, Mourinho brought a printout of two incidents he felt should have resulted in dismissals: a clash between Cristian Romero and Jude Bellingham, and a challenge from Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde.
fullText:
La Liga president Javier Tebas says claiming referees are directed against Real Madrid is "living in another galaxy" as the fallout continued from José Mourinho blaming officials for making key errors in their 2-1 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Sunday.

At the post-match press conference, Mourinho brought a printout of two incidents he felt should have resulted in dismissals: a clash between Cristian Romero and Jude Bellingham, and a challenge from Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde.

Mourinho felt Atlético should have been reduced to nine players before Dean Huijsen was sent off for Los Blancos five minutes after the interval for bringing down Giuliano Simeone, resulting in a spot-kick which Alejandro Grimaldo put away.

Jonathan David added a second shortly after and Antonio Rüdiger's late goal was nothing but a consolation as Real Madrid suffered their second defeat of the campaign.

After the game, Real Madrid – now six points behind Barcelona heading into the international break – echoed Mourinho's views in a website match report headlined: "A dreadful refereeing performance decides the derby".

Atlético responded with a social media post showing Mourinho at his press conference, with the caption 'Stop referee harassment now' – and, in a clear dig at the Portuguese, an accompanying video of the image coming out of a printer.

In a lengthy post on X, Tebas referenced a Spanish media article which questioned referee impartiality and that the championship had already been decided, insisting there was no "conspiracy".

"All clubs can be officiated by international referees and by those who aren't. None has the right to on-demand refereeing," Tebas said.

"Real Madrid is crucial to La Liga. But claiming that 'La Liga is worth nothing' without it reveals the disdain for the other clubs, their fans, and their history. The competition belongs to no one.

"Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy. That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.

"It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch.

"And my stance doesn't depend on any position: a refereeing error doesn't prove a conspiracy, nor does repeating it for years turn it into truth.

"Get the blindfold off! It's September, and they are already calling the league adulterated. No one with common sense buys that old excuse anymore."

title: Hibs must strike fine balance in managerial appointment
description: It was good to get Saturday's game out the way after a difficult couple of weeks at Hibs.  It felt like full-time properly brought the curtain down on (Sir) David Gray's tenure, even if the separation had formally happened a few days earlier, and the club now have the luxury of a bit of break in which to recruit a new head coach.  The team are scheduled to head to Spain for a training break - an incoming head coach could use this as a mini-pre-season with time to convey their ideas and tactics without the pressure of managing a game-to-game schedule.
fullText:
It was good to get Saturday's game out the way after a difficult couple of weeks at Hibs.

Easter Road was quite subdued before kick-off and I think most fans will agree the break has come at a good time for the club.

There was a notable lifting of tensions around the stadium, in stark contrast to the charged atmosphere on Tuesday where the team was chastised for any and every mistake by sections of the crowd.

It felt like full-time properly brought the curtain down on (Sir) David Gray's tenure, even if the separation had formally happened a few days earlier, and the club now have the luxury of a bit of break in which to recruit a new head coach.

The team are scheduled to head to Spain for a training break - an incoming head coach could use this as a mini-pre-season with time to convey their ideas and tactics without the pressure of managing a game-to-game schedule.

We can now look forward with some optimism and excitement. The club need to get this appointment right and there's a fine balance between reading the room in terms of gauging supporter sentiment and being brave enough to back whoever they identify as Gray's successor, even if it's not a universally popular choice.

This is where Malky Mackay and the recruitment team have to earn their corn. The assumed benefit of having a sporting director is to minimise disruption when a head coach leaves, so hopefully Gray's successor is announced sooner rather than later.

You can find Matty Fairnie at Longbangers podcast

title: Israel accuse Ireland manager of ‘hypocrisy and stupidity’ over ‘genocide’ comments
description: The Israel Football Association have reacted furiously after Heimir Hallgrimsson said the Republic of Ireland will be ‘playing against genocide’ ahead of the upcoming games between the two countries
fullText:
The Israel Football Association accused Republic of Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson of "hypocrisy and stupidity" after he said his team would be "playing against genocide" in their upcoming Uefa Nations League double header between the two teams.

Ireland have been drawn in the same Nations League group as Israel and the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) have confirmed that they will fulfill both fixtures despite mounting calls from campaigners to boycott the games, which will be taking place in neutral venues in Hungary and Serbia due to safety concerns. The first game will be held in Hungary on 27 September.

In comments made over the weekend following the announcement of Ireland's squad, Hallgrimsson admitted that "none of us feel comfortable playing in these games". When asked how his players can focus on the fixtures given the calls to boycott the games back home, Hallgrimsson added: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

In a furious response on social media on Monday night, the Israel FA wrote: "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way. Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

The FAI has not responded to the Israel FA's comments.

The Israeli government has vehemently denied the charges of genocide since their retaliation to the October 7 attacks almost three years ago, when about 1,200 people were killed by Hamas and 250 people were taken hostage. Over 70,000 Palestinians have since been killed in the war in Gaza, according to figures used by the United Nations.

We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way. Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We’re not playing with…

The FAI previously said that refusing to play against Israel would have a "profound impact on the whole of Irish football", arguing that forfeiting Nations League points could weaken their chances of qualifying for Euro 2028, when they will be co-hosts, as well as future World Cups.

The FAI wrote to Uefa last November calling for the immediate suspension of the Israel FA, and has since lodged a request with Uefa to separate the Republic of Ireland from Israel in future draws. The FAI said the request was denied because the two countries have "never been in direct conflict".

A Uefa spokesperson said: "Decisions to avoid certain teams being drawn against each other are made taking into consideration several factors, especially conditions between the two countries leading to structural risks for security. Uefa handles every situation very carefully on its own merits and monitors all facts and developments."

Meanwhile, a group of over 160 Irish sportspeople have signed an open letter issued by the Irish Sport for Palestine Group urging the FAI to reconsider its previous decision to go ahead with the fixtures.

The letter reads: "This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing. Not playing the game would be the most sporting thing you could do."

Former Republic star Kevin Kilbane added his voice to the protests, writing in the Irish Times: "Ireland should not be playing Israel. Not in Dublin, not in Hungary, and definitely not a 'home' match in Serbia. Not while Israeli forces are committing genocide.

"We as Irish people could have faced down the consequences together. The FAI would have had my support as a former international."

A group gathered outside the team's hotel in Dublin on Monday evening, urging the FAI to reverse its decision to proceed with the fixture.

title: ACC/SEC Challenge Details Set. Here’s Our First Look
description: This is just a first look. We’ll get into the deets later.
fullText:
ESPN released the dates, times and networks for this year's ACC/SEC Challenge on Monday, which are listed below. Here's our first take on what we think will happen. We'll likely revisit this by late November.

BC at Georgia – as of now, we'd have to take Georgia, but if the Eagles start hot, we might reconsider.

FSU at Tennessee. We'll probably regret this, but we'll take Florida State for now. Luke Loucks has proven a lot already, and now he's got an imposing big man who Rick Barnes would love to have for the Vols. If he stays out of foul trouble, he could pound Tennessee inside.

Auburn at Clemson. We don't know a lot about Auburn yet, but Littlejohn is no joke. We'll go with the Tigers – the ACC Tigers, that is.

South Carolina at NC State. State is likely to be better coached, and it's in Raleigh, so we'll back the Pack here.

Pitt at Missouri. We'll have to go with Mizzou here. Regrettably, but it's the truth.

Arkansas at UNC. Wow, interesting, right? The Hogs should have the talent, but UNC still has mystique. Talent usually wins out, so Arkansas.

Texas at Louisville. This one is interesting too. We don't know a ton about UT yet, but as of now, they appear even, so we'll go with the home team.

Syracuse at Oklahoma. Another interesting matchup. Porter Moser has underperformed at OU, but we don't know much about his team yet. We'll stick with the home team here, at least until we know more.

Ole Miss at Virginia Tech. Chris Beard really damaged his career in Austin when he was arrested for allegedly assaulting his former fiancée. However, he can still coach. We'll take the Rebels here.

Wake Forest at LSU. This one is tough, because no one knows who Will Wade will have on his roster. Our gut says LSU, but they'll need more bodies, and Wade seems determined to fight the SEC, and he could get suspended if it comes to that. We'll have to revisit.

Duke at Florida. We don't bet against Duke.

Kentucky at Virginia. Historically, you'd default to Kentucky, but Mark Pope has not yet proved himself, and Ryan Odom certainly has. We'll ride with who? Why the 'Hoos, of course.

Vanderbilt at Notre Dame. There's no particular reason to favor Notre Dame over Vandy. There's just not.

Alabama at Miami. This one should be really good. When in doubt, go with defense. Therefore: Miami.

Stanford at Texas A&M. BuckyBall vs. NerdBall. We'll have to go with the home team here, mostly because Stanford has a lot to prove.

Georgia Tech at Mississippi State. Scott Cross is just getting started, but the bottom fell out at Mississippi State last year. Everyone will probably still be geeking out over the football team, so Tech might have a chance. But we'll go with the Bulldogs for now.
